metadata.title: AI Stack Map — 11-Category Product Research
metadata.scope: Data only. Covers the full AI stack from model datasets to user-facing applications.

categories.parity_verdict: OSS has reached near-parity with closed-source in coding agents — OpenHands, Aider, Cline, and Goose rival Cursor and Devin on benchmarks — but closed-source products still lead in polish, vertical integration, and enterprise adoption.

Open-weights base models have moved from 'near-parity' to 'co-leading' the frontier in 2026. Llama 5 (600B+, 5M context, April 2026), DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T MoE, 1M context, MIT, April 2026), Mistral Large 3 (675B MoE, Apache 2.0, December 2025), Qwen3.5 (397B-A17B, Apache 2.0), and GLM-4.6 (355B MoE, MIT, September 2025) now match closed flagships (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Muse Spark) on most standard coding and reasoning evals. The shifts that matter: (1) the GLM-4 line flipped fully open in 2025, removing one of the last 'closed Chinese frontier' holdouts; (2) Cohere's Command A+ (May 2026) joined as the first fully Apache 2.0 enterprise frontier model from a Western lab; (3) DeepSeek-R2 (32B dense, MIT, 92.7% AIME 2025, runnable on a single 24GB consumer GPU — see Cat 3) directly inverts the 'bigger is better' reasoning thesis and shows that the open camp is now leading on efficiency, not just catching up on scale. Closed models retain narrow leads at the absolute top of LMArena (Claude Opus 4.6/4.7 at Elo 1498-1502 vs Muse Spark at 1489 and Gemini 3.1 Pro at 1488, all within CI of each other) and on emerging multimodal-agent tasks (computer use, 35-hour autonomous runs). But on raw capability per benchmark, the open vs closed gap at the base-pretrained layer has effectively closed — for the first time, the strategic question is no longer 'when will open catch up' but 'which side is winning each specific axis.'

Open-source has crossed parity at the frontier in 2026 H1. DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1M context, MIT, open weights) sits in the SWE-bench top-10 alongside Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI flagships, and DeepSeek-R2 — a 32B dense MIT model that runs on a single 24GB consumer GPU and hits 92.7% AIME 2025 — inverted the 'bigger MoE wins reasoning' thesis that anchored the 2024–2025 narrative. Kimi K2.6 (1T MoE), Qwen3-Coder-Next, and GLM-4.6 round out a credible four-way open-weight frontier. Closed models still hold advantages in agent scaffolding maturity, long-horizon tool-use reliability, and computer-use visual acuity (Opus 4.7 at 98.5%), and a leaked Claude Mythos Preview (93.9% SWE-bench Verified) suggests the next closed-weight tier is already trained. Net: parity on raw eval scores; meaningful closed-model lead on agentic reliability and integrated tool ecosystems.

Open leads decisively. The top three serving engines (vLLM, llama.cpp, SGLang) are all open-source and dominate production deployments. Closed players differentiate on custom hardware (Groq LPU, Cerebras wafer-scale) or managed convenience (Azure, AWS), not on software superiority. Open-source inference code is the clearest open-wins category in the entire stack.

OSS dominates fine-tuning code — TRL, Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory, Unsloth, PEFT, and verl together cover SFT/LoRA/QLoRA/DPO/RLHF/GRPO at parity or better than any closed offering; closed-source platforms compete on managed convenience and proprietary model access (GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini) rather than capability.

Open-source dominates the eval-harness category — every widely-used benchmark runner (SWE-bench, lm-evaluation-harness, Inspect AI, OpenCompass, Promptfoo, DeepEval) is OSS, with closed offerings mostly differentiating via managed dashboards, proprietary judge models, and private benchmark sets rather than the harness itself.

Open-source owns the primitives — Firecracker, gVisor, Kata Containers underlie nearly every closed sandbox. But the managed-sandbox-for-agents experience is led by closed offerings (Modal $4.65B valuation, Replit $9B, Vercel Sandboxes, Cloudflare Workers) that out-scale open-core options like E2B and Daytona on UX, observability, and reliability — and the gap is widening, not narrowing.

Open-source has reached genuine parity in the self-hosted chat-UI segment (Open WebUI, LibreChat, Lobe Chat, AnythingLLM rival ChatGPT's UX) and dominates the API-gateway tier (LiteLLM, Helicone), but closed players still own the mass-market consumer surface — ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Grok command billions of users that no open frontend approaches.

Competitive — open-source tools (Langfuse, Phoenix, Opik) offer full-featured tracing, cost tracking, and prompt analytics on par with closed alternatives. LangSmith leads on LangChain ecosystem lock-in and Datadog on enterprise APM integration, but OSS options are self-hostable and increasingly the default for startups.

Open-dominant — benchmark datasets are overwhelmingly open by nature, since benchmarks only work if everyone can run them. Closed entries are limited to proprietary internal test suites and contamination-resistant services that withhold problems. Open datasets define the field.

Open leads on protocols and retrieval — MCP is the de facto standard and the top vector DBs are all open-source. Closed leads on search APIs where Tavily, Exa, and Perplexity offer curated, agent-optimized results that no open equivalent matches. Browser tooling is converging: Playwright MCP (open) competes head-to-head with Browserbase (closed), though managed cloud browsers still have an edge on anti-bot handling.

OSS has reached near-parity with closed-source in coding agents — OpenHands, Aider, Cline, and Goose rival Cursor and Devin on benchmarks — but closed-source products still lead in polish, vertical integration, and enterprise adoption.
coverage_gaps: Non-coding autonomous agents (eg sales, customer support) are underrepresented in OSS
Enterprise workflow orchestration agents are mostly closed-source
Multi-agent coordination at scale remains nascent in both segments

products.description: Open-source autonomous coding agent (formerly OpenDevin) that can write code, run commands, browse the web, and interact with APIs to complete software engineering tasks end-to-end. Differentiates through a sandboxed execution environment and strong SWE-bench performance, consistently ranking among the top open-source agents. 74.5K GitHub stars with 460+ contributors and extremely active development (710+ commits in 90 days).
products.classification_rationale: Takes a goal (GitHub issue, task description), autonomously plans steps, executes code and shell commands, and iterates until the task is complete — core agent loop behavior.

products.description: Terminal-based AI pair programming tool that edits code directly in your local git repo. Differentiates through deep git integration (automatic commits with sensible messages), support for 20+ LLM providers, and a sophisticated diff-based editing approach that minimizes token usage. 45K GitHub stars; widely regarded as the benchmark for CLI-based coding agents and the tool that pioneered the 'agentic coding in terminal' pattern.
products.classification_rationale: Receives a coding goal in natural language, plans file edits, executes changes across multiple files, runs tests, and iterates — autonomous multi-step agent behavior.

products.description: Autonomous coding agent available as a VS Code extension, CLI tool, and SDK. Can create and edit files, run terminal commands, use the browser, and orchestrate multi-step development tasks with human-in-the-loop approval. Differentiates through its IDE-native experience and extensible SDK for embedding agent capabilities into other products. 62K GitHub stars with 1,078 commits in 90 days, one of the fastest-growing coding agent projects.
products.classification_rationale: Takes a development goal, autonomously plans and executes file edits, terminal commands, and browser actions — textbook orchestration agent with tool use.

products.description: Research-driven autonomous coding agent from Princeton NLP that takes a GitHub issue and attempts to automatically fix it using LLMs. Also supports offensive cybersecurity and competitive coding challenges. Published at NeurIPS 2024 and served as an early benchmark-setter for the SWE-bench leaderboard. 19.3K stars with 92 contributors; development pace has slowed in 2026 (16 commits in 90 days) but the project remains influential as a reference architecture.
products.classification_rationale: Receives a GitHub issue as a goal, autonomously navigates the codebase, plans edits, applies patches, and validates fixes — autonomous agent loop.

products.description: Open-source extensible AI agent from Block (fka Square) that goes beyond code suggestions to install packages, execute commands, edit files, and run tests with any LLM. Differentiates through first-class MCP (Model Context Protocol) support and a Rust-based core for performance. 45.7K GitHub stars with 452 contributors and 918 commits in 90 days — one of the most actively developed open-source agents, backed by a major tech company.
products.classification_rationale: Accepts a goal, plans multi-step execution, calls tools (shell, file system, browser, APIs via MCP), and iterates autonomously.

products.description: Lightweight open-source coding agent from OpenAI that runs in your terminal. Built in Rust for speed, it reads your codebase, proposes a plan, and executes multi-file changes with sandboxed command execution. Differentiates as OpenAI's official open-source agent offering (Apache-2.0) with tight integration to OpenAI models. 84.6K GitHub stars with an extraordinary 2,893 commits in 90 days and 454 contributors — the most rapidly developed OSS agent as of May 2026.
key_dependencies: OpenAI API (primarily, though supports other providers)
products.classification_rationale: Takes a coding task, plans steps, executes file edits and shell commands in a sandboxed environment, and iterates until completion — autonomous agent loop.

products.description: One of the earliest and most well-known autonomous AI agent platforms, AutoGPT lets users define goals and the agent recursively breaks them into sub-tasks, executes actions, and learns from results. Has evolved from a viral demo into a more mature platform with a visual builder and marketplace. 184K GitHub stars (highest in the category) with 429 contributors, though much of the star count reflects the 2023 hype wave. Still actively developed with 668 commits in 90 days.
products.classification_rationale: The canonical example of an orchestration agent — receives a high-level goal, autonomously decomposes it, executes tools, and iterates toward completion.

products.description: Open-source agent framework that makes websites accessible to AI agents, enabling autonomous web browsing, form filling, data extraction, and multi-step online task completion. Built on Playwright, it provides a structured way for LLMs to observe page state, plan actions, and execute browser interactions. 95K GitHub stars with 315 contributors — one of the fastest-growing projects in the agent space, filling the crucial gap of web-native agent capabilities.
products.classification_rationale: Receives a web-based task goal, autonomously plans navigation steps, executes browser actions, observes results, and iterates — agent loop applied to web automation.

products.description: Autonomous research agent that conducts deep web research on any topic by planning research queries, browsing multiple sources, synthesizing findings, and generating comprehensive reports. Differentiates as a purpose-built research agent (not coding-focused) that orchestrates search, scraping, and synthesis into a coherent workflow. 27.2K GitHub stars with 210 contributors; an early mover in the 'deep research' agent pattern that inspired similar features in ChatGPT and Gemini.
products.classification_rationale: Takes a research question as a goal, autonomously plans queries, searches the web, reads and synthesizes sources, and produces a structured report — multi-step autonomous agent.

products.description: Open-source generalist AI agent positioned as an 'autonomous company operating system' — can browse the web, write and execute code, manage files, interact with APIs, and complete complex multi-step business tasks. Differentiates through an ambitious scope beyond coding (document creation, data analysis, web research) with a polished web UI. 19.8K GitHub stars with explosive development velocity (2,522 commits in 90 days), suggesting heavy investment in rapid iteration.
products.classification_rationale: Accepts high-level business goals, autonomously plans and executes multi-tool workflows (code, browser, file system, APIs) — generalist orchestration agent.

products.description: Agentic coding tool from Anthropic that lives in the terminal, understands your entire codebase, and autonomously executes multi-step development tasks including code generation, refactoring, git workflows, and testing. Differentiates through deep integration with Claude models, a rich skill/hook system for customization, and native MCP tool support. 125.7K GitHub stars; source-available but not open-source (no license). Reportedly the fastest-growing developer tool in Anthropic's portfolio.
products.classification_rationale: Takes a development goal, autonomously plans multi-step execution, reads/writes files, runs commands, manages git, and iterates — the defining example of a terminal-based orchestration agent.

products.description: AI-first code editor (VS Code fork) with an integrated agent mode that can autonomously make multi-file changes, run terminal commands, and iterate on code based on errors. Differentiates through seamless IDE integration where the agent works alongside manual editing, plus frontier model access and a background agent feature for asynchronous task completion. Reportedly 100K+ paying users at ~$20/month, making it the most commercially successful AI coding tool outside GitHub Copilot. Raised $900M+ at a $9B+ valuation.
products.classification_rationale: Agent mode takes a goal, plans multi-file edits, executes terminal commands, and iterates on errors autonomously — orchestration agent embedded in an IDE.

products.description: The first product marketed as a fully autonomous AI software engineer. Operates in a cloud-based sandboxed environment with its own shell, browser, and editor, completing entire development tasks from specification to pull request. Differentiates as the highest-profile 'autonomous developer' product with full environment access rather than just file editing. Raised $175M at a $2B valuation; commercially available via API and web interface, though real-world performance reviews are mixed compared to initial demo claims.
products.classification_rationale: Receives a software engineering task, autonomously plans implementation, writes code, debugs, and submits PRs — the canonical closed-source orchestration agent for coding.

products.description: Google's agent-first developer platform — launched as a standalone IDE in November 2025 (public preview competing with Cursor), then expanded at Google I/O in May 2026 into Antigravity 2.0 with a Go-based CLI, SDK, and multi-agent orchestration. The CLI replaces Gemini CLI (which sunsets for free tiers in June 2026). Powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash with deep Google Cloud / Firebase / Android integration.
products.classification_rationale: Takes development goals and autonomously plans, executes code changes, runs commands, and iterates — agent-mode IDE in the same category as Cursor and Claude Code.

products.description: AI-native IDE (VS Code fork) with 'Cascade' — an agentic flow engine that maintains context across multi-step coding tasks, automatically suggests and executes terminal commands, file edits, and debugging steps. Differentiates through 'Flows' that blend co-pilot suggestions with autonomous agent actions, plus strong context awareness across large codebases. Reportedly millions of users across free and paid tiers; Codeium raised $150M at a $1.25B valuation before being acquired by Windsurf (the brand name superseded Codeium).
products.classification_rationale: Cascade mode takes a goal and autonomously plans multi-step code changes, runs commands, and iterates on errors — IDE-embedded orchestration agent.

products.description: AWS's AI-powered development assistant with an autonomous agent mode that can implement features, fix bugs, write tests, and perform code transformations across entire codebases. Differentiates through deep AWS service integration (can deploy, debug Lambda functions, query CloudWatch) and enterprise security features. Available in IDE extensions, CLI, and AWS Console; included in AWS enterprise agreements, giving it a large potential installed base.
products.classification_rationale: Agent mode receives a development task, autonomously plans implementation across files, executes changes, runs tests, and iterates — orchestration agent with cloud-native integration.

products.description: GitHub Copilot's agent mode transforms the autocomplete assistant into an autonomous coding agent that can plan multi-step implementations, edit files across a project, run terminal commands, and iterate on test failures. Differentiates through the deepest GitHub platform integration (issues, PRs, Actions, code review) and the largest existing user base (~1.8M paid subscribers as of early 2026). Copilot Workspace extends this with a cloud-based planning environment for issue-to-PR workflows.
products.classification_rationale: Agent mode accepts a task, autonomously plans and executes multi-file changes, runs commands, tests, and iterates — GitHub's entry in the orchestration agent space.

products.description: Cloud-based autonomous development agent embedded in Replit's online IDE that can build entire applications from natural language descriptions — scaffolding projects, installing packages, writing code, configuring databases, and deploying to production. Differentiates through zero-setup cloud execution (no local environment needed) and end-to-end deployment capability, making it the most accessible agent for non-developers. Replit has 30M+ registered users; raised $200M+ total funding.
products.classification_rationale: Receives a high-level app description, autonomously plans architecture, generates code, configures infrastructure, and deploys — full-stack orchestration agent.

products.description: AI-powered generative UI and full-stack development agent from Vercel that builds web applications from natural language prompts. Can autonomously generate React/Next.js components, assemble full pages, manage state, connect to APIs, and iterate based on visual feedback. Differentiates through frontend-first design quality and tight Next.js/Vercel deployment integration. Evolved from a UI generation tool into a full autonomous development agent in 2025.
products.classification_rationale: Takes an app or UI description, autonomously plans component architecture, generates code, previews results, and iterates — orchestration agent specialized for frontend/full-stack development.

products.description: AI-powered full-stack development agent that builds production-ready web applications from natural language descriptions, handling everything from UI design to backend logic and database setup. Evolved from the open-source GPT Engineer project into a polished commercial product. Differentiates through a visual development experience where users can iterate on a live preview, plus integrated deployment and Supabase backend integration. Raised $25M; growing rapidly in the 'vibe coding' category alongside v0 and Bolt.
products.classification_rationale: Takes an app description as a goal, autonomously plans architecture, generates full-stack code, deploys previews, and iterates based on user feedback — end-to-end orchestration agent.

products.description: Consumer-facing 'Personal Intelligence' agent — a multi-platform (web, macOS, iOS, CLI) assistant with episodic, semantic, and procedural memory that takes actions on the user's behalf. Pivoted in 2026 from an LLMops/prompt-engineering platform (prompts, workflows, evals) to a consumer agent product after a $20M Series A in July 2025; legacy LLMops surface still available but no longer the headline.
products.classification_rationale: 2026 hero positioning is 'Your Personal Intelligence' — a consumer agent product that takes goals and autonomously executes multi-step tasks across web/macOS/iOS. Per the litmus test 'does this product take a goal and figure out the steps itself?' — yes. Belongs in Orchestration Agents, not in Evaluation Code where the legacy LLMops platform once lived.

products.description: Minimal code-first agent framework from Hugging Face (~1,000 lines of core code) whose headline CodeAgent writes actions as executable Python rather than JSON tool calls, which research shows uses ~30% fewer steps than traditional tool-calling agents on hard benchmarks. Differentiates through model-agnostic design (Hugging Face Inference, OpenAI, Anthropic, local transformers/llama.cpp) and first-class MCP support, making it the path of least resistance for HF users building agents. 27.5K GitHub stars, 203 contributors, Apache-2.0; featured in Hugging Face's official agents course and referenced in Anthropic and Cohere agent-building guides.
key_dependencies: LLM endpoint (Hugging Face Inference, OpenAI, Anthropic, local transformers)
Python sandbox (local or E2B for safe execution)
products.classification_rationale: Cat 1 litmus 'AI in the driver's seat?' returns yes — CodeAgent receives a goal, plans steps as code, executes in a sandbox, observes outputs, and iterates autonomously. Not Cat 11 because smolagents is the agent runtime, not a tool an external agent calls.

products.description: Enterprise agent platform for building, deploying, orchestrating, and governing AI agents that reason and act with company context. Glean frames the product around agent builder, agent orchestration, agent library, agentic engine, deployment, and observability, and it publicly announced a horizontal agent platform with dozens of agents and open interoperability across the enterprise.
products.classification_rationale: The product’s headline promise is autonomous agents that plan and execute work across workflows, which matches Cat 1.

products.description: Open-source autonomous agent that grows with the user through persistent memory, reusable skills, and a built-in learning loop. It runs on a VPS or serverless backend, can be controlled through Telegram and other messaging surfaces, and is designed to keep improving over long-lived sessions rather than acting as a one-shot chat wrapper. Scale signal: the Hermes Agent repo is MIT-licensed, has 163k+ GitHub stars, and shows very heavy recent development activity.
products.classification_rationale: The product’s own positioning emphasizes an autonomous agent with a learning loop, persistent memory, and self-improvement over time — not a human-driven chat UI, inference engine, or tool protocol.

products.description: Open-source personal AI agent (CLI + runtime) that runs on a user's own devices, with browser control, filesystem access, shell execution, persistent memory, and 6 messaging frontends (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, iMessage). Model-agnostic (Claude / GPT / local). Started by Peter Steinberger in Nov 2025 as Clawdbot; launched as OpenClaw Jan 2026; community-led foundation after Steinberger joined OpenAI Feb 2026. Sponsors include OpenAI, NVIDIA, GitHub, Vercel.
key_dependencies: LLM endpoint (Claude, GPT, or local model)
products.classification_rationale: Autonomous personal agent: takes natural-language goals from messaging-app interfaces, plans multi-step actions, executes across browser/files/shell, and iterates with memory — core orchestration-agent loop applied to a personal-assistant (rather than coding) use case.
