categories.thin_segment_note: The closed-source segment is inherently thin for BASE pretrained models. Most closed providers only expose instruction-tuned endpoints via API. The 'base model' listed for each closed provider is the underlying pretrained model family that powers their API products, but users cannot access the raw base weights. Several entries (Reka, AI21, Cohere, Inflection) are included as meaningfully distinct model families, but the boundary between 'base pretrained' and 'instruction-tuned API' is blurry for closed models since all API access is to post-trained versions.

products.description: Meta's open-weights foundation model family in 8B, 70B, and 405B parameter variants that established the open-source ecosystem baseline. Trained on 15T+ tokens with grouped query attention and a 128K context window under the Llama Community License. Superseded by Llama 4 (April 2025) and Llama 5 (April 2026), but still the most widely adopted historical baseline — the 8B variant alone retains roughly 5M monthly Hugging Face downloads and remains the default seed for community fine-tunes.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights are available for download on HuggingFace separate from the Instruct variants. The base model has not been instruction-tuned or RLHF'd.

products.description: Meta's previous-generation open-weights model family (April 2025), introducing mixture-of-experts to the Llama line: Llama 4 Scout (17B active / 109B total, 16 experts, 10M token context) and Llama 4 Maverick (17B active / 400B total, 128 experts). The planned Llama 4 Behemoth was reportedly abandoned in favor of Llama 5. Superseded by Llama 5 (April 2026) but remains an important architectural reference for sparse-MoE open weights.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights released on HuggingFace. The base (non-instruct) variants are available for download without instruction tuning.

products.description: Meta's current open-weights flagship, released April 8, 2026. 600B+ parameters with a 5M-token context window, trained on a 500K-Blackwell-B200 cluster — the largest training run for an open-weights model to date. Includes a 'Llama Guard 4' safety layer. Zuckerberg positioned Llama 5 as matching or exceeding GPT-5 and Gemini 3 on reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks at release. Maintains the Llama Community License and remains the anchor of the open-weights frontier, although the Meta Superintelligence Labs sibling 'Muse Spark' has taken the closed-API flagship role.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights distributed on Hugging Face separately from any Instruct variant; the underlying pretrained checkpoint is available without instruction tuning. Cat 2 litmus test ('have these weights been post-trained for a downstream use?') returns no for the base release.

products.description: Legacy 671B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (37B active per token) trained on 14.8T tokens with FP8 mixed precision at a reported ~$5.5M training cost. Shifted the narrative on cost-efficient frontier model training when released in December 2024, and remained the open-weights reference point through most of 2025. Superseded by DeepSeek-V4-Base (April 2026); the hosted `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` aliases deprecate 2026-07-24, but V3 weights remain widely fine-tuned in the community.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights available on HuggingFace. DeepSeek-V3-Base is the raw pretrained checkpoint before any instruction tuning or RLHF alignment.

products.description: DeepSeek's current open-weights flagship, released April 24, 2026 in two variants: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T total / 49B active parameters) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B total / 13B active). Both support a 1M default context window (384K max output) and dual Thinking / Non-Thinking modes. V4-Pro requires only 27% of V3.2's inference FLOPs and 10% of the KV cache at 1M tokens — a major efficiency leap. Released with full open weights under MIT license on Hugging Face. The hosted `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` aliases deprecate 2026-07-24 as V3 is retired.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights distributed on Hugging Face under MIT license. The DeepSeek-V4 base checkpoint is available without instruction tuning, separate from the chat/reasoner instruct variants. Cat 2 litmus passes.

products.description: Alibaba's Apache-2.0 open-weights family (0.5B-72B dense plus a 57B-A14B MoE) trained on 18T+ tokens, with specialist code and math variants. Now the previous-generation Qwen line — superseded by Qwen3 (April 2025) and Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.7-Max (2026) — but still the most-downloaded non-Western open model: the 2.5 lineup recorded 750M+ Hugging Face downloads in 2025 and over 113K Qwen-derivative models now exist on the Hub, anchored largely by 2.5's 7B variant.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights available on HuggingFace without instruction tuning. Separate Instruct variants exist for the chat-tuned versions.

products.description: Alibaba's current open-weights flagship line, launched April 28, 2025 under Apache 2.0. Includes six dense models (0.6B / 1.7B / 4B / 8B / 14B / 32B) and two MoE variants (30B-A3B and 235B-A22B), trained on 36T tokens. Introduced hybrid reasoning — a single model that exposes both 'Thinking' (chain-of-thought) and 'Non-Thinking' (fast-response) modes via a runtime switch. Extended in 2025-2026 with Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (ultra-sparse MoE with hybrid attention, September 2025), Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.5-Plus (February 16, 2026 — 397B-A17B Apache 2.0), and Qwen3.7-Max (May 20-21, 2026 — Alibaba's proprietary 'agent-era' flagship, #1 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 57, capable of 35-hour autonomous runs and 1000+ tool calls). Qwen3.7-Max is closed-weights, signalling a hybrid open/closed strategy.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained Qwen3 weights distributed on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0, separate from Instruct variants. Cat 2 applies to the base pretrained checkpoints; Qwen3.7-Max specifically is closed, but the entry represents the open-weights Qwen3 line as the canonical base.

products.description: Mistral AI's 123B-parameter dense model (July 2024, 128K context) under the Mistral Research License — Europe's flagship open-weights frontier model at release, fluent across nine languages and strong on code/math. Retired and replaced by Mistral Large 3 on 30 March 2025; relevant historically but no longer the active SKU. Mistral overall reported ~450K customers and $400M+ ARR by mid-2025.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights available for download. Mistral releases both base and instruct variants separately.

products.description: Mistral AI's first mixture-of-experts model since Mixtral and the current open-weights flagship, released December 2, 2025 under Apache 2.0. 41B active / 675B total parameters, 256K context, native multimodal support (text + images). Trained from scratch on 3000 H200 GPUs. Debuted at #2 on the LMArena OSS non-reasoning leaderboard. Combined with Ministral 3 (smaller dense variants) and Mistral Vibe CLI in the broader Mistral 3 stack. Runs at the compute cost of a ~41B dense model while accessing the capacity of a 675B one — Europe's flagship open-weights frontier model and the direct successor to the retired Mistral Large 2 (March 2025).
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights released on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0, separate from instruction-tuned variants. Cat 2 litmus passes — raw pretrained checkpoint is available.

products.description: Google's previous-generation open-weights model family (2B/9B/27B) derived from Gemini research, using knowledge distillation from larger models during training. Released July 2024 under the Gemma license; now superseded by Gemma 3 (March 2025) which added multimodal vision capability. Gemma 2 9B remains widely used as a community fine-tuning base, with ~1.5M monthly Hugging Face downloads on the base 9B variant.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights available on HuggingFace and Kaggle. Gemma 2 base models are not instruction-tuned; separate '-it' (instruction-tuned) variants exist.

products.description: Google's current open-weights model family, released March 12, 2025 — and the first open-weights Gemma generation with native vision-language capability. Available in 1B/4B/12B/27B variants (the 1B is text-only; the 4B/12B/27B are vision-language models), with a 128K context window on the larger variants and native multilingual support for 140+ languages. The Gemma 3 27B fits at Q4 on a single 3090 yet competes with much larger 400B-600B models on standard evals. Released under the Gemma license on Hugging Face and Kaggle. Google's primary contribution to the open-weights ecosystem in 2025-2026.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights distributed on Hugging Face and Kaggle without instruction tuning. Separate '-it' (instruction-tuned) variants exist. Cat 2 litmus passes.

products.description: Microsoft's 14B-parameter small language model that punches well above its weight class on reasoning, math, and code — released December 2024 under MIT license. Trained on heavily curated and synthetic data, demonstrating the 'small models with high-quality data' thesis. As of May 2026 the Phi-4 line is still current: Microsoft has extended it with Phi-4-mini, Phi-4-multimodal, and Phi-4-reasoning / Phi-4-reasoning-plus (May 2025), plus Phi-4-reasoning-vision-15B (March 2026). No Phi-5 has been announced.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights released on HuggingFace. Phi-4 base is available separately from any instruction-tuned variant.

products.description: TII's open-weights model line from Abu Dhabi. The original Falcon 3 family (1B/3B/7B/10B Apache-2.0, December 2024) has been extended in 2025-2026 by Falcon-H1 — a hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture spanning 0.5B-34B with native 18-language support — and Falcon-H1 Arabic (3B/7B/34B, January 2026), positioned as the world's leading Arabic open model. Falcon H1R 7B (January 2026) outperforms Qwen and Nemotron variants up to 7x its size on reasoning. Adoption remains modest vs Llama/Qwen at equivalent size (Falcon3-7B-Instruct ~23K monthly HF downloads).
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights available on HuggingFace. Falcon 3 base models are released separately from instruction-tuned variants.

products.description: Kai-Fu Lee's 01.AI foundation model family in 6B, 9B, and 34B variants, with continued pretraining on 500B tokens over Yi-1.0. Strong performance on Chinese and English benchmarks. Apache 2.0 licensed. One of the top Chinese-origin open-weights models, though increasingly competing with Qwen for mindshare in the Chinese open-source community.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights available on HuggingFace. Yi base models are released without instruction tuning.

products.description: Shanghai AI Lab's open-weights model family. The InternLM 2.5 generation (7B/20B, July 2024, 1M context via dynamic NTK interpolation) was superseded by InternLM3 in January 2025 — an 8B model trained on only 4T tokens that reportedly matches GPT-4o-mini, with integrated 'deep thinking' chain-of-thought mode and ~4x the data efficiency (IQPT) of Llama 3.1. A leading Chinese academic-origin foundation model, heavily used in the Chinese research community.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights available on HuggingFace. InternLM2.5-7B-Base is the non-instruction-tuned variant.

products.description: EleutherAI's suite of 16 models ranging from 70M to 12B parameters, all trained on the same data (The Pile) in the same order, with intermediate checkpoints released throughout training. Designed as a scientific tool for studying how language models learn, not for production use. Fully open (model, data, training code, intermediate checkpoints). The gold standard for LLM interpretability and scaling research.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights only — no instruction tuning was performed. The entire point of the suite is to provide clean base model checkpoints for research.

products.description: OpenAI's legacy multimodal foundation model (May 2024) that natively handled text, image, and audio. Now two numerical generations behind: superseded by the GPT-5 line (GPT-5 in August 2025, then 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, and GPT-5.5 on April 23, 2026 — the first fully retrained base since GPT-4.5). All access remains API-only via post-trained variants; GPT-4o is being sunset as the ChatGPT default in favor of GPT-5.5 Instant (May 5, 2026). Listed as the historical closed-source baseline that open-weights models were measured against through 2024-2025.
products.classification_rationale: The base pretrained model exists internally at OpenAI but is never exposed directly. All API access is to instruction-tuned variants. Listed here as the closed counterpart representing the underlying foundation model capability.

products.description: OpenAI's April 2025 model update optimized for coding, instruction following, and long-context tasks (1M token window), available in full/mini/nano variants. Now superseded by the GPT-5 line; GPT-4.1 is still available via API but is no longer OpenAI's flagship. The o-series reasoning brand has been folded into GPT-5 (GPT-5.5 reasoning replaces the o-series role). Notable as the last GPT-4-family base model before the GPT-5 retraining.
products.classification_rationale: Closed-source base model powering API endpoints. No weights distributed. All access is through instruction-tuned API.

products.description: OpenAI's current closed foundation model line: GPT-5 (August 2025), then post-training iterations GPT-5.2, 5.3, 5.4, and finally GPT-5.5 (April 23, 2026) — the first fully retrained base since GPT-4.5. GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5 Pro shipped via API on April 24, 2026; GPT-5.5 Instant became the default ChatGPT model on May 5, 2026, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant. The o-series reasoning brand has been folded into the GPT-5 line. GPT-5.5 is positioned as 'smartest and most agentic' with major gains in agentic coding, computer use, and knowledge work. API-only — no weights distributed; the base pretrained model is never exposed directly. The benchmark closed-source frontier that open-weights models are measured against in 2026.
products.classification_rationale: Closed base pretrained model. No weights distributed — all access is through post-trained API endpoints. Listed in Cat 2 as the closed-source frontier counterpart to open-weights bases like Llama 5 and DeepSeek V4, paralleling how GPT-4o was previously listed.

products.description: Anthropic's frontier closed-weights base model (April 2026), the largest tier in the Claude 4.x line. The base is never exposed directly — all access is to the Constitutional-AI + RLHF post-trained variant (Claude Opus 4.7), which tops SWE-bench Verified at 87.6% and holds two of the top four LMArena Elo slots (1492-1502). A leaked 'Claude Mythos Preview' trained on the same family reportedly hits 93.9% SWE-bench Verified. Direct competitor to GPT-5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on the agentic-coding frontier.
products.classification_rationale: Closed-source base model. No weights distributed. Anthropic has never released pretrained weights or exposed the base model through API. All access is to post-trained (Constitutional AI + RLHF) variants.

products.description: Anthropic's mid-tier closed-weights base model (February 2026), the workhorse of the Claude 4.x line and the most widely deployed variant in production agents. The base is never exposed directly — only the post-trained Sonnet 4.6 ships via API, where it sits within 1pp of Opus 4.7 on SWE-bench Verified (79.6%) and holds top-tier LMArena Elo. Optimized for cost-per-quality at scale; the default Claude tier in Cursor, Claude Code, and most coding-agent deployments.
products.classification_rationale: Closed-source base model. No weights distributed. Anthropic has never released pretrained weights or exposed the base model through API. All access is to post-trained (Constitutional AI + RLHF) variants.

products.description: Google's natively multimodal foundation model family handling text, image, video, audio, and code in a unified architecture. As of May 2026 the current line is Gemini 3 Pro, Gemini 3.1 Pro (preview — leading LiveCodeBench Pro at 2887 Elo), Gemini 3 Flash, and Gemini 3.5 Flash (launched at I/O 2026 on May 19, 2026, now the default in the Gemini app). Gemini 3.5 Pro arrives June 2026. Context windows up to 2M tokens. The base model is never exposed directly — all access is through post-trained API endpoints; Gemma serves as Google's open-weights counterpart.
products.classification_rationale: Closed-source base model. No weights distributed. Google releases Gemma as its open-weights offering (listed separately above), while the full Gemini model remains API-only.

products.description: Cohere's enterprise foundation model line, currently anchored by Command A+ (released May 20, 2026) — a 218B-parameter sparse MoE (25B active) with native citation generation, W4A4 lossless quantization, and the company's first fully Apache 2.0 licensed frontier model. Runs on a single B200 or two H100s. Positioned for sovereign AI and enterprise RAG with native support for 48 languages and explicit grounding spans linking every factual claim to source documents. Earlier Command R+ (104B, 2024) is the predecessor; with Command A+ the line has flipped from API-only to open-weights.
products.classification_rationale: While early Command R models had open weights, Command R+ is primarily API-only in practice. The base pretrained model is not separately accessible from the instruction-tuned API. Listed as closed due to practical access constraints.

products.description: Elon Musk's xAI foundation model family powering Grok on X. Grok-1 (314B MoE) weights were open-sourced in March 2024 (Apache 2.0); all subsequent versions are API-only. Current is Grok 4.20 / Grok 4.20 Heavy (February 2026) — a multi-agent architecture using 4 specialized sub-agents (Captain, Harper, Benjamin, Lucas) in the base tier and 16 specialized agents in the Heavy tier ($300/month SuperGrok Heavy). The internal peer-review loop reportedly cut hallucination rates from ~12% to ~4.2%. Grok 5 (claimed 10T parameters) is still in training as of May 2026. Trained with real-time X firehose data as a differentiated source.
products.classification_rationale: Grok-1 base weights were released (Apache 2.0) but Grok-2/3 are closed. Listed as closed because the current frontier version is API-only with no weight distribution.

products.description: Amazon's in-house foundation model family on AWS Bedrock. Originally launched December 2024 (Nova Micro/Lite/Pro), then extended in April 2025 with Amazon Nova Premier (1M context, designed as a 'teacher' for model distillation). The Nova 2 family was announced at AWS re:Invent 2025 — Nova 2 Lite (cost-effective reasoning), Nova 2 Pro (most intelligent tier, in preview for Nova Forge customers), and Nova 2 Sonic (speech-to-speech). All Nova 2 models support up to 1M tokens of context with 65K-token responses. Amazon's play to reduce dependence on Anthropic and Meta within its own cloud stack; closed-source, Bedrock-only.
products.classification_rationale: Closed-source model accessible only through AWS Bedrock API. No weights distributed. The base pretrained model is not separately accessible.

products.description: Reka AI's multimodal foundation model that natively processes text, images, video, and audio (128K context). Founded by ex-DeepMind / Google / Meta researchers, Reka Core was originally pitched as a GPT-4V / Claude 3 Opus / Gemini Ultra rival. The company has since extended the stack with Reka Flash 3 (open-weights, 2025) and Reka Nexus (a multi-agent 'AI workforce' product). Reka Core remains API-only as the closed flagship; no verified 2026 successor to Core itself was found in this audit, though the surrounding product line has evolved.
products.classification_rationale: Closed-source model. API-only access. No weights distributed. The base pretrained model is not separately accessible.

products.description: AI21's hybrid SSM-Transformer architecture combining Mamba state-space layers with Transformer attention and mixture-of-experts. The original Jamba 1.5 (August 2024, 52B active / 398B total, 256K context) was succeeded by Jamba 1.6 (Mini and Large, March 2025) and Jamba 2 (Jamba2 Mini at 12B active, January 2026, plus Jamba2 3B for on-device / agentic systems). Jamba remains the only frontier-class model line using a non-pure-Transformer architecture; Jamba 1.5 Mini and Jamba 2 Mini are Apache 2.0 open weights while Jamba Large is API-only.
products.classification_rationale: Jamba 1.5 Mini weights are open (Apache 2.0) but Jamba 1.5 Large is API-only. The flagship model is closed-source, accessible only through AI21's API.

products.description: Inflection AI's foundation model powering the Pi assistant and the company's enterprise 'Inflection for Enterprise' tier. After key staff (Mustafa Suleyman et al.) departed to Microsoft AI in March 2024, Inflection pivoted to enterprise. Inflection 3.0 is the current flagship — powered by Intel Gaudi 3 with on-prem or AI Cloud deployment options; no new generation publicly confirmed by May 2026. Notable as a case study in foundation-model market concentration dynamics: pace has slowed dramatically post-pivot.
products.classification_rationale: Closed-source model. API-only access through Inflection for Enterprise. No weights distributed.

products.description: Zhipu AI's foundation model family, originating from Tsinghua University research. GLM-4 (closed-source, 2024) competed with GPT-4 on Chinese benchmarks, but the line has since flipped open: GLM-4.5 (July 2025) and GLM-4.6 (September 30, 2025) ship with MIT-licensed open weights. GLM-4.6 is a 355B-parameter MoE with a 200K context window and published CC-Bench trajectories on Hugging Face. Z.ai's GLM-4.6V (vision variant) released later in 2025. The 'GLM-4 is API-only' positioning is no longer accurate.
products.classification_rationale: Originally classified as closed, but GLM-4.5 (July 2025) and GLM-4.6 (Sept 2025) ship with MIT-licensed open weights on Hugging Face. The product entry now covers the line as it stands in mid-2026: open-weights base model with separate API offering. Cat 2 applies because base pretrained weights are downloadable without instruction tuning.

products.description: Zhipu AI's current frontier model, released September 30, 2025 — a 355B-parameter MoE with MIT-licensed open weights, a 200K context window, and published CC-Bench evaluation trajectories on Hugging Face for independent verification. Builds on GLM-4.5 (July 2025) and represents Zhipu's pivot to a fully open-weights frontier strategy. Z.ai (Zhipu's international brand) has also debuted GLM-4.6V, a native tool-calling vision variant. Deployable locally via vLLM or SGLang. Marks a sharp contrast with the prior closed-source GLM-4 positioning and one of the cleanest signals that Chinese frontier models have moved decisively open in 2025-2026.
products.classification_rationale: Base pretrained weights distributed on Hugging Face under MIT license. Cat 2 litmus passes — raw pretrained checkpoint is downloadable independently of any instruction-tuned variant.

categories.parity_verdict: Open-source has crossed parity at the frontier in 2026 H1. DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1M context, MIT, open weights) sits in the SWE-bench top-10 alongside Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI flagships, and DeepSeek-R2 — a 32B dense MIT model that runs on a single 24GB consumer GPU and hits 92.7% AIME 2025 — inverted the 'bigger MoE wins reasoning' thesis that anchored the 2024–2025 narrative. Kimi K2.6 (1T MoE), Qwen3-Coder-Next, and GLM-4.6 round out a credible four-way open-weight frontier. Closed models still hold advantages in agent scaffolding maturity, long-horizon tool-use reliability, and computer-use visual acuity (Opus 4.7 at 98.5%), and a leaked Claude Mythos Preview (93.9% SWE-bench Verified) suggests the next closed-weight tier is already trained. Net: parity on raw eval scores; meaningful closed-model lead on agentic reliability and integrated tool ecosystems.
coverage_gaps: Emerging Chinese closed-source coding models (Baichuan, MiniMax) are underrepresented due to limited English-language benchmarking
Specialized code models for non-English programming ecosystems may be missed

products.description: Mixture-of-experts coding model family (30B-A3B and 480B-A35B variants, plus the newer Qwen3-Coder-Next built on Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B with hybrid attention) instruction-tuned for agentic coding. Qwen3-Coder-Next achieves 70%+ on SWE-bench Verified via SWE-Agent scaffold and is the current dedicated open-weight coder flagship; the 30B-A3B variant retains 1.6M+ monthly downloads. Note: as of May 2026 there is no Qwen3.5-Coder or Qwen3.7-Coder — Qwen3.7-Max is text-only and closed-weight.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained MoE weights specifically tuned for code generation and agentic tool use via instruction tuning and RLHF.

products.description: Dense coding model family (1.5B to 32B) instruction-tuned for code completion, generation, and chat. The 32B variant was the strongest open-source coding model through most of 2025, with strong performance across HumanEval, MBPP, and LiveCodeBench. The 7B variant alone has 2.4M+ monthly downloads.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned dense transformer weights specifically post-trained for code generation and coding chat.

products.description: Instruction-tuned 14B Qwen2.5 chat model for general assistant workloads — distinct from the Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct variant in covering broader chat and reasoning rather than code-specialized output. Apache 2.0 license, 128K context, and competitive scores against Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct on reasoning and multilingual evals at a fifth the size. Pulls ~2.5M Hugging Face downloads per month, making it the most-adopted mid-size open instruct checkpoint from a non-US lab.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained weights optimized for dialogue, instruction following, and assistant-style responses.

products.description: Previous-generation reasoning-first model (January 2025) using large-scale GRPO RL to develop chain-of-thought before answering. 671B MoE plus 1.5B–70B distilled variants. Superseded by DeepSeek-R2 (April 2026), which inverts the architecture thesis — R2 is a 32B dense MIT model that runs on a single 24GB consumer GPU and reaches 92.7% AIME 2025. R1 retains 4.3M+ monthly downloads and remains the most-used open reasoning model.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained via large-scale RL (GRPO) to produce reasoning chains for code and math tasks — a distinct form of post-training beyond standard instruction tuning.

products.description: Previous-generation general-purpose instruction-tuned MoE model (671B total / 37B active). Still widely used (4.2M+ monthly downloads) but superseded by DeepSeek-V4-Pro / V4-Flash (April 2026, 1M default context, 384K max output). The legacy `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` aliases route to V4-Flash from 2026-07-24.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned and RLHF'd MoE weights optimized for chat, coding, and general tasks.

products.description: Dedicated coding MoE model (seed product) instruction-tuned for code generation, completion, and chat. Available in full (236B) and Lite (16B) variants. The Lite variant remains popular for local deployment with 1.1M+ downloads. Predecessor to the V3/R1 generation that proved open-source could compete on coding benchmarks.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned MoE weights specifically post-trained for code generation tasks.

products.description: DeepSeek's open-weight April 2026 flagship line, replacing V3.2. Released 2026-04-24 with 1M default context and 384K max output. V4-Pro-Max posts 80.6% on SWE-bench Verified (top-10) and a later snapshot reports 93.5% on LiveCodeBench. Available via the `deepseek-chat` (V4-Flash) and `deepseek-reasoner` aliases from 2026-07-24, with weights on Hugging Face under MIT. Demonstrates that open weights can match closed-API frontier coding performance at the same context window.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned and RLHF'd MoE weights optimized for chat, coding, and long-context tasks — Cat 3 litmus (post-trained for a downstream use) returns yes.

products.description: Parity-shifting open-weight reasoning model released April 2026 — a 32B dense MIT-licensed model that hits 92.7% AIME 2025 and runs on a single 24GB consumer GPU. Inverts the prior 'bigger MoE is better' reasoning thesis established by R1 (671B MoE) by showing a much smaller dense architecture can match or exceed cloud-hosted closed reasoning models on math/coding evals. Treated by many observers as the single most important open-vs-closed development of 2026 H1.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained via large-scale RL for reasoning chains on math and coding — same Cat 3 classification as R1, but a distinct architectural product (dense, not MoE).

products.description: Code-specialized instruction-tuned Llama 2 family (7B to 70B, seed product) trained on 500B+ tokens of code and fine-tuned for coding chat. Pioneered the open-source coding LLM wave in 2023 and catalyzed the entire open code model ecosystem. Still used as a baseline with ~104K combined monthly downloads across sizes.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned Llama 2 weights specifically post-trained on code corpora for code generation and chat.

products.description: Instruction-tuned 8B Llama 3.1 model for chat and assistant workflows, post-trained with SFT and DPO on Meta's Llama 3.1 base. The 128K context window and Llama Community License made it the default open instruct checkpoint for production chat deployments. Currently the most-downloaded Llama variant on Hugging Face at ~10.8M downloads/month, surpassing every other open chat checkpoint by an order of magnitude.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained Llama weights optimized for instruction following and conversational use.

products.description: Mistral's dedicated open-weight agentic coding model family, purpose-built for software engineering tasks including SWE-bench. The Small-2 (24B) instruct variant delivers competitive coding performance in a deployable size with 321K downloads. The larger Devstral-2-123B pushes frontier-class performance under a research license.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned weights specifically post-trained for agentic software engineering and code generation.

products.description: Instruction-tuned 7B chat model from Mistral that follows user prompts in a dialogue format. It was the first widely adopted European open instruct release (Dec 2023) and remains the canonical 7B chat baseline in eval papers and fine-tuning tutorials. Still pulls ~3.2M Hugging Face downloads per month nearly 2.5 years after release.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained weights optimized for chat and instruction following, not a base pretrained checkpoint.

products.description: Open-science code model family (3B, 7B, 15B, seed product) trained on The Stack v2 with 619 programming languages. A collaborative project between HuggingFace and ServiceNow representing the most transparent large-scale code model training effort. Serves as a foundation for community instruction-tuned variants; the 3B model has 113K monthly downloads.
products.classification_rationale: While the base weights are pretrained, the official and community instruct variants qualify as finetuned chat. Included as the canonical open-science code model that spawned many instruction-tuned derivatives.

products.description: Compact instruction-tuned small language model (3.8B) that punches well above its weight on coding benchmarks. Part of Microsoft's Phi-4 family, which expanded across 2025–early 2026 with Phi-4-reasoning, Phi-4-multimodal, and Phi-4-Reasoning-Vision-15B (March 2026); no Phi-5 has shipped as of May 2026. 1.6M monthly downloads make Phi-4-mini one of the most popular small models for local coding.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned small language model weights post-trained for coding, reasoning, and chat tasks.

products.description: IBM's enterprise-focused open-source code model line, now folded into the unified Granite 4.1 family (3B, 8B, 30B dense, base + instruct, Apache-2.0) released April 29, 2026. Granite 4.1 delivers significant improvements over Granite 4.0 in tool calling, instruction following, coding, and math, while preserving IBM's IP-clean training-data provenance — still the go-to choice for enterprises needing legal clarity on training data. Available on watsonx and Hugging Face.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned transformer weights post-trained specifically for enterprise code generation tasks.

products.description: Previous reasoning tier (2025): full-scale o3 plus cost-efficient o4-mini, both using extended chain-of-thought. Powered Codex agent and ChatGPT's coding mode through 2025. Folded into the GPT-5 line in late 2025 — OpenAI consolidated the o-series and GPT branches and is no longer maintaining o-series as a separately branded reasoning family. Current reasoning capability lives in GPT-5.x with thinking enabled and in GPT-5.3-Codex.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained via reinforcement learning for reasoning and coding; weights are not distributed but the model represents distinct post-training beyond the GPT-4 base.

products.description: Previous-generation general-purpose instruction-tuned model (April 2025). Strong on HumanEval and real-world coding with 1M token context, but two numerical generations behind by mid-2026 — OpenAI's current production line is GPT-5 → 5.2 → 5.4 → 5.5 (April 23, 2026), with GPT-5.5 Pro and 5.5 Instant variants. GPT-4.1 remains available via API and is still used in legacy integrations.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned and RLHF'd model weights optimized for coding and chat tasks.

products.description: OpenAI's current general-purpose flagship line spanning GPT-5 (August 2025), GPT-5.2, GPT-5.4, and GPT-5.5 (April 23, 2026), plus the GPT-5.5 Pro (API-only flagship), GPT-5.5 Instant (low-latency consumer tier), and GPT-5.3-Codex (the unified Codex+reasoning coder variant that succeeded o3/o4-mini). GPT-5.5 is marketed as OpenAI's 'smartest, most agentic' model; GPT-5.2 hits 80.0% on SWE-bench Verified and GPT-5.5 reportedly reaches 88.7% on a competing benchmark snapshot. GPT-5.5-high sits at #8 on the May 2026 LMArena text leaderboard (Elo 1481). Note: OpenAI has reportedly stopped reporting SWE-bench Verified scores, preferring SWE-bench Pro, citing test-case quality issues with Verified.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned and RLHF'd flagship line optimized for chat, coding, agentic tool use, and reasoning. Reasoning capabilities from the o-series are folded into 5.x with thinking enabled. Cat 3 litmus (post-trained for downstream use) returns yes.

products.description: Previous-generation Sonnet tier (May 2025). Strong on SWE-bench Verified and agentic tool use with extended thinking mode and 200K context, but superseded by Sonnet 4.5 (2025-09-29) and Sonnet 4.6 (2026-02-17), which is the current production default coding tier. Sonnet 4.7 was skipped per leaked Claude Code source; Sonnet 4.8 is the next planned tag.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained via RLHF and Constitutional AI for conversational coding and agentic tasks.

products.description: Anthropic's heavy-reasoning Opus tier, tuned for sustained agentic coding and long-horizon planning across large codebases. Opus 4 scored 72.5% on SWE-bench Verified at release (May 2025 era); the line has iterated through Opus 4.5 (80.9%), Opus 4.6 (80.8%), and Opus 4.7 (April 2026), which hits 87.6% SWE-bench Verified and 98.5% computer-use visual acuity. Opus 4.6 and 4.7 are tied at the top of LMArena (Elo ~1500). A leaked 'Claude Mythos Preview' tops SWE-bench at 93.9% and is presumed to be the next-generation Opus / Claude 5 candidate.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained via RLHF and Constitutional AI, specifically tuned for complex reasoning and agentic coding.

products.description: Anthropic's current production default coding tier (released 2026-02-17), following Sonnet 4 (May 2025) and Sonnet 4.5 (Sept 2025). Posts 79.6% on SWE-bench Verified (top-10) with extended thinking mode and 200K context (1M in beta). Powers Claude Code CLI and most enterprise coding deployments where Opus 4.7 is reserved for the hardest agentic tasks. Sonnet 4.7 was skipped; Sonnet 4.8 is the next planned tag per leaked source.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained via RLHF and Constitutional AI for conversational coding and agentic tasks — Cat 3 litmus returns yes.

products.description: Anthropic's small/fast tier in the Claude 4 generation, designed for high-volume low-latency coding and chat workloads. Sits beneath Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.7 in capability but at substantially lower cost — the default Anthropic option for embedded agents, autocompletion, and high-QPS production routes. Released alongside the Sonnet 4.5/4.6 cadence as Anthropic's three-tier lineup (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) stabilized at the 4.x generation.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained for chat and coding at the small/fast tier — Cat 3.

products.description: Previous-generation Gemini Pro tier (2025) with native multimodal understanding, 1M+ token context, and hybrid thinking mode. Superseded by Gemini 3 Pro and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, which leads LiveCodeBench Pro at 2887 Elo and posts 80.6% on SWE-bench Verified. Gemini 3.5 Pro is expected June 2026. 2.5 Pro remains available via Google AI Studio and Vertex AI for cost-conscious workloads.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained multimodal model with instruction tuning and RLHF for chat, coding, and reasoning tasks.

products.description: Previous-generation speed-optimized model (2025) with configurable thinking budgets. Superseded by Gemini 3 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash (May 19, 2026), the new default in the Gemini app — 'Pro-grade reasoning at Flash-level speed,' #9 on the May 2026 LMArena text leaderboard (Elo 1480) and #2 on LiveCodeBench at 90.8%. 2.5 Flash remains a popular cost-tier for high-volume deployments.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned and RLHF'd distilled model weights optimized for efficient coding and chat.

products.description: Google's current top-coding-tier closed model. Leads LiveCodeBench Pro at 2887 Elo, posts 80.6% on SWE-bench Verified (#5 on the May 2026 leaderboard) and 88.5% on LiveCodeBench, with native multimodal understanding and a 1M+ token context window. Sits at #6 on the May 2026 LMArena text leaderboard (Elo 1488) — effectively tied with Claude Opus 4.6/4.7 within the 95% CI. Gemini 3.5 Pro is expected June 2026.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained multimodal model with instruction tuning and RLHF for chat, coding, and reasoning — Cat 3 litmus returns yes.

products.description: Released at Google I/O 2026 (May 19, 2026) as the new default in the Gemini app. Marketed as 'Pro-grade reasoning at Flash-level speed' — #9 on the May 2026 LMArena text leaderboard (Elo 1480) and #2 on LiveCodeBench at 90.8%. Configurable thinking budgets let users trade reasoning depth for latency. Powers Antigravity / Gemini CLI and most Google-side coding-assistant deployments where cost matters.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned and RLHF'd distilled model optimized for efficient coding and chat — Cat 3.

products.description: Previous-generation xAI flagship (February 2025), trained on the 100K-H100 Colossus cluster. Superseded by Grok 4, Grok 4.1, and Grok 4.20 Heavy (Feb 2026) — the latter uses a 16-agent specialized system. Grok 5 is still in training (claimed 10T params; ~33% chance of release by 2026-06-30 per prediction markets). Grok 3 remains available via X platform integration.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained model weights tuned for conversational coding and agentic tasks via instruction tuning and RLHF.

products.description: xAI's current flagship instruction-tuned product (Feb 2026), built as a 16-agent specialized system — multiple Grok-4 instances coordinated around specialized roles rather than a single monolithic call. Marketed as xAI's top reasoning + agentic tier; ships alongside Grok 4 and Grok 4.1 as the standard API tiers. Grok 5 is still in training (claimed 10T params; ~33% chance of release by 2026-06-30 per prediction markets).
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained model weights (and orchestrated multi-agent system) tuned for conversational coding and agentic tasks. The headline product is the instruction-tuned model line, not a separable agent framework, so Cat 3.

products.description: Mistral's proprietary code model, API-only via la Plateforme, Vertex AI, Azure AI Foundry, and Bedrock. Current SKU is Codestral 25.08 (August 2025) — 30% more accepted completions and 50% fewer runaway generations versus 25.01. Part of Mistral's broader 2026 coding stack alongside Codestral Embed (retrieval-tuned embeddings), Devstral 2 (open-weight agentic coding counterpart), and Mistral Vibe CLI (Mistral's answer to Claude Code / Gemini CLI). Distributed to thousands of developers through Continue.dev, JetBrains, and VS Code integrations; reported usage trails Anthropic and OpenAI coding models.
products.classification_rationale: Proprietary instruction-tuned model weights post-trained specifically for code generation, not distributed as open weights.

products.description: Amazon's proprietary multimodal model line in AWS Bedrock. Current flagship is Amazon Nova 2 Pro (preview), launched at re:Invent 2025 (December 2, 2025) alongside Nova 2 Lite (speed/cost tier), Nova 2 Omni (unified text/image/video/audio in + text/image out), and Nova 2 Sonic (speech-to-speech). Nova 2 Pro emphasizes agentic capability gains over the original Nova line. No 'Nova 2 Premier' exists as of May 2026 — Nova 2 Pro is the top-tier model. Competitive pricing for high-volume AWS-native enterprise deployments with SLA guarantees.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned model weights post-trained for coding, chat, and enterprise tasks.

products.description: Zhipu AI's flagship instruction-tuned model line, now at GLM-4.6 (late 2025) following GLM-4.5 (July 2025). Strong multilingual coding (especially Chinese-English) with 128K+ context and native tool use. Notable structural shift: GLM-4.5 and 4.6 ship open-weights variants (a reversal of the GLM-4 API-only stance) — Zhipu now competes directly in the open-weight frontier alongside DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi. Widely deployed in Chinese enterprise environments via API and self-hosted weights.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned and RLHF'd model weights post-trained for conversational coding and general tasks.

products.description: Meta Superintelligence Labs' flagship closed-weight API model, launched April 2026. Closed top-5 on the May 2026 LMArena text leaderboard (Elo 1489) — the first non-Anthropic/Google/OpenAI model to break the top 5 in 2026. Represents Meta's parallel closed-weights track alongside the open-weights Llama line (Llama 5, April 2026), effectively splitting Meta into two flagship brands. Chat/instruction-tuned tier sits in Cat 3 alongside other API-only frontier models.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned closed-weight chat model competing at the API tier — Cat 3. The base pretrained variant would go in Cat 2.

products.description: Moonshot AI's open-weight 1T-parameter MoE released 2026-04-20 under a Modified MIT license, with 256K context. Top-10 on SWE-bench Verified at 80.2% and ties GPT-5.4 on agentic/coding benchmarks. Notable for a 300-sub-agent / 4000-step swarm capability — Moonshot ships native multi-agent scaffolding with the weights. One of the four credible open-weight frontier contenders (alongside DeepSeek V4, Qwen3-Coder-Next, and GLM-4.6) for chat/coding workloads in 2026.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned and RLHF'd 1T MoE weights optimized for chat, coding, and agentic tasks — Cat 3.

products.description: MiniMax's flagship instruction-tuned coding model, top-10 on SWE-bench Verified at 80.2% as of May 2026. Part of the wave of Chinese frontier-tier coding models (alongside DeepSeek V4, Kimi K2.6, Qwen3-Coder-Next, and GLM-4.6) closing the gap with Anthropic/Google/OpenAI on standard coding evals. Available via MiniMax's hosted API with multi-modal extensions.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained instruction-tuned model for chat and coding — Cat 3 litmus returns yes.

products.description: ByteDance's flagship closed-weight instruction-tuned model line, released February 14, 2026 in four variants (Pro, Lite, Mini, Code) via the Volcano Engine API. The Pro tier ($0.47 input / $2.37 output per million tokens) posts frontier-tier benchmarks — 98.3 AIME 2025, 88.9 GPQA Diamond, 76.5 SWE-Bench Verified, 3020 Codeforces — at 3.7×–10× lower cost than GPT-5.2 / Claude Opus 4.5. Differentiates on (a) Chinese-language strength and Volcano Engine's mainland-China-native infrastructure, (b) aggressive price-to-performance positioning, and (c) deep distribution via the Doubao consumer chat app, which crossed 100M DAU in early 2026 and reached ~345M MAU by March 2026 — the largest consumer AI chat product in China. Doubao Seed 1.6 (October 2025, 256K context) remains in the lineup as the budget tier; ByteDance ships 19 active Doubao API SKUs in 2026.
products.classification_rationale: Instruction-tuned and RLHF'd closed-weight chat/coding model served via API — Cat 3 litmus returns yes. The Doubao consumer app surface belongs in Cat 8 and should be added separately.

products.description: NVIDIA's first-party open-weight instruction-tuned model family for agentic reasoning, post-trained with SFT + RL on top of Nemotron Base. Current SKUs are Nemotron 3 Nano (30B total / 3B active hybrid MoE, March–April 2026) and Nemotron 3 Super (120B / 12B active Mamba-Transformer MoE, March 11, 2026); Nemotron 3 Ultra (~500B / 50B active) is announced for H1 2026. Differentiates on (a) open training data and recipes published alongside the weights, (b) 1M-token context with strong RULER scores (Super 91.8 @ 1M), and (c) being NVIDIA's reference post-trained line for NeMo and NIM — optimized end-to-end against NVIDIA hardware. Adoption signal: 1.38M monthly Hugging Face downloads on Nano BF16 plus 758K on Super BF16, and free hosting on OpenRouter and build.nvidia.com.
key_dependencies: NVIDIA NeMo / NIM stack (recommended deployment path)
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained (SFT + RL) instruction-tuned weights with reasoning-traces capability — Cat 3 litmus returns yes. The companion Nemotron-3-*-Base variants are the Cat 2 counterpart.

products.description: Hybrid-mode reasoning model built on ByteDance Seed-OSS-36B-Base. Nous frames it as roughly matching Hermes-4-70B performance at half the size; the public Hugging Face checkpoint has 6.4K cumulative downloads and 209 likes, making it the current flagship 36B release.
products.classification_rationale: It is a post-trained chat/reasoning checkpoint, not a base model or serving runtime.

products.description: Frontier hybrid-mode reasoning model built on Meta-Llama-3.1-405B. It is the largest Hermes 4 variant in the public release set, with 1.1K cumulative downloads and 269 likes on Hugging Face.
products.classification_rationale: This is a post-trained checkpoint on top of a named base model, so it belongs with other finetuned/chat weights.

products.description: Smaller Hermes 4 hybrid-mode reasoning model built on Meta-Llama-3.1-70B. The public checkpoint has 1.9K cumulative downloads and 126 likes, positioning it as the mid-size option in the Hermes 4 family.
products.classification_rationale: It is a post-trained checkpoint rather than a serving runtime or base model.

products.description: Small dense Hermes variant for local inference and low-cost deployment. The model card shows 2.8K cumulative downloads and 146 likes, making it the most lightweight Hermes 4 checkpoint in the public lineup.
products.classification_rationale: It is a finetuned checkpoint, not an inference server or chat UI.

products.description: A 1.1B instruction-tuned chat model from the TinyLlama project, built on the Llama architecture and trained on 3T tokens for ~90 days on 16 A100-40G GPUs. It became the canonical sub-2B open chat baseline for edge and local-inference research and still pulls ~2.5M Hugging Face downloads per month two years after release.
products.classification_rationale: Post-trained for conversational instruction following and chat, so it fits the Finetuned Chat bucket.

categories.parity_verdict: Open leads decisively. The top three serving engines (vLLM, llama.cpp, SGLang) are all open-source and dominate production deployments. Closed players differentiate on custom hardware (Groq LPU, Cerebras wafer-scale) or managed convenience (Azure, AWS), not on software superiority. Open-source inference code is the clearest open-wins category in the entire stack.
coverage_gaps: Diffusion/image model inference engines (e.g., TensorRT for Stable Diffusion) not covered — scoped to LLM/text generation
Audio/speech inference runtimes (Whisper.cpp exists but omitted as niche)
Embedded/microcontroller inference (TFLite Micro, etc.) excluded — different hardware tier
categories.thin_segment_note: The closed-source side is structurally thin on pure inference code because the core software innovation happens in open-source. Closed entries are either (a) custom-silicon vendors whose value is the hardware, not the software, or (b) cloud providers wrapping open engines behind managed APIs. Very few companies ship proprietary inference runtimes that compete with open alternatives on software merit alone.

products.description: High-throughput LLM serving engine built on PagedAttention, which treats KV cache as virtual memory pages to near-eliminate memory waste during batched inference. Supports continuous batching, tensor parallelism, speculative decoding, and 40+ model architectures. The de facto standard for self-hosted production model serving — used by Anyscale, Databricks, and most open-source inference deployments.
products.classification_rationale: Loads model weights and serves inference requests via OpenAI-compatible API. Core function is turning weights into fast API responses with GPU memory optimization.

products.description: CPU and GPU inference engine for LLMs written in portable C/C++. Pioneered the GGUF quantization format (2-8 bit) that became the ecosystem standard for local model distribution. Runs on consumer hardware — laptops, phones, Raspberry Pi — without requiring CUDA or Python. 112K+ GitHub stars make it the most-starred inference project; foundational infrastructure that powers Ollama, LM Studio, GPT4All, and dozens of other tools.
products.classification_rationale: Loads quantized model weights and runs inference directly. The quintessential 'load weights, serve predictions' project.

products.description: High-performance LLM/VLM serving engine built around RadixAttention for automatic prefix-KV reuse, with structured-generation, speculative decoding, and disaggregated-prefill support. Deployed on 400K+ GPUs worldwide and serving trillions of tokens/day; xAI uses it to serve Grok 3, Microsoft Azure to serve DeepSeek R1 on AMD, and adopters include AMD, NVIDIA, AWS, Oracle Cloud, LinkedIn, and Cursor. Joined the PyTorch ecosystem in March 2025; 28K GitHub stars with 450+ contributors.
products.classification_rationale: Loads model weights and serves inference with an emphasis on structured generation performance. Pure inference serving engine.

products.description: Hugging Face's production LLM serving solution, purpose-built for the HF model ecosystem. Supports continuous batching, tensor parallelism, Flash Attention, and quantization (GPTQ, AWQ, EETQ). Powers Hugging Face Inference Endpoints and is the default backend when deploying models from the Hub. Tight integration with the transformers library makes it the path of least resistance for HF users going to production.
products.classification_rationale: Loads model weights from HF Hub and serves inference requests. Core function is model serving with HF ecosystem integration.

products.description: Local LLM runtime that wraps llama.cpp in a user-friendly CLI and REST API with a Docker-like model management experience (ollama pull, ollama run). Handles model downloading, quantization selection, and GPU/CPU routing automatically. 172K GitHub stars — the most popular way for developers to run models locally. Became the default local inference backend for dozens of AI applications and MCP integrations.
products.classification_rationale: Loads model weights and serves local inference. Built on llama.cpp but adds model management, API server, and hardware abstraction.

products.description: NVIDIA's optimized LLM inference library providing maximum throughput on NVIDIA GPUs through kernel fusion, in-flight batching, FP8/INT4 quantization, and multi-GPU tensor parallelism. Python API for defining and compiling models into optimized TensorRT engines. Used by major cloud providers and inference services as the backend for NVIDIA GPU deployments. Source code is Apache-2.0, but the value proposition is tightly coupled to NVIDIA hardware and CUDA ecosystem.
products.classification_rationale: Compiles and serves LLM inference with hardware-specific optimizations. Core function is turning model weights into optimized GPU inference engines.

products.description: Cross-platform inference accelerator supporting models from PyTorch, TensorFlow, and other frameworks via the ONNX interchange format. Runs on CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, and custom accelerators with hardware-specific execution providers. Used in production across Microsoft products (Windows, Office, Azure). Unique differentiator: hardware-agnostic — one runtime targets NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Qualcomm, and Apple silicon. 20K+ stars, steady development over 7+ years.
products.classification_rationale: Loads model weights (in ONNX format) and runs inference across hardware platforms. General-purpose inference runtime, not LLM-specific but widely used for transformer inference.

products.description: Toolkit for compressing, deploying, and serving LLMs with a focus on high throughput on NVIDIA GPUs. Features TurboMind engine with persistent batch scheduling, blocked KV cache, and efficient quantization (W4A16, W8A8). Strong support for Chinese-ecosystem models (InternLM, Qwen, ChatGLM). Used in production by Shanghai AI Lab and related research organizations. Growing alternative to vLLM in the Chinese developer ecosystem.
products.classification_rationale: Loads model weights, applies quantization, and serves inference. Core function is optimized LLM serving.

products.description: Distributes LLMs as single executable files that run on six operating systems (Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD) without installation. Uses Cosmopolitan libc to create fat binaries containing both the model weights and inference runtime. Built on llama.cpp internals. The unique value proposition is zero-dependency distribution — download one file, run it, get an inference server. 24K+ stars despite niche positioning.
products.classification_rationale: Packages model weights with an inference runtime into a single executable. Core function is loading weights and serving predictions with zero setup.

products.description: Unified inference engine built on the Mojo programming language that targets multiple hardware backends (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple) from a single codebase. Includes a graph compiler that automatically optimizes model execution for the target hardware. Supports PyTorch and Hugging Face models with claimed performance matching or exceeding TensorRT-LLM on NVIDIA GPUs while also running on non-NVIDIA hardware. Founded by former LLVM/Swift creator Chris Lattner. 26K+ stars on the combined Modular repo.
products.classification_rationale: Loads model weights and optimizes inference execution across hardware targets. Core function is high-performance model serving with hardware abstraction.

products.description: Inference service running on custom Language Processing Unit (LPU) hardware designed from the ground up for sequential token generation. Achieves industry-leading token throughput — widely benchmarked at 500-800 tokens/sec for Llama-class models, far exceeding GPU-based alternatives. Deterministic, SRAM-based architecture eliminates memory bottlenecks. Available via API with OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The company that put 'inference speed' in the mainstream conversation in early 2024.
products.classification_rationale: Custom hardware + proprietary runtime that loads model weights and serves inference. The LPU architecture and compiler are fully proprietary.

products.description: Inference service running on the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE-3), a single chip containing 4 trillion transistors with 44GB of on-chip SRAM — eliminating off-chip memory bottlenecks entirely. Achieves extremely high throughput on large models by keeping the entire model on a single wafer. Available via API. Positioned as the fastest inference for large models where the entire model fits on one wafer. Raised $4.3B+, filed for IPO.
products.classification_rationale: Custom wafer-scale hardware + proprietary runtime serving model inference. The hardware architecture, compiler, and serving runtime are all proprietary.

products.description: High-performance inference platform built on a proprietary FireAttention engine optimized for multi-tenant model serving on commodity GPUs. Specializes in efficiently serving many models and LoRA adapters simultaneously with minimal overhead. Supports open models (Llama, Mixtral, Qwen) and function calling. Founded by ex-Meta PyTorch team members. Competitive pricing and low latency have made it a popular choice for startups building on open models.
products.classification_rationale: Proprietary inference engine that loads model weights and serves predictions. The FireAttention kernel and multi-model serving infrastructure are closed-source.

products.description: Proprietary inference engine optimized for serving open-source models at scale with Flash Attention, speculative decoding, and custom CUDA kernels. Supports a wide catalog of open models with fast switching. Also offers a dedicated endpoints product for reserved GPU capacity. Founded by researchers from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU. Differentiated by combining inference speed with strong research output (RedPajama, Together MoE research).
products.classification_rationale: Proprietary inference runtime serving open-weight models. The core engine, scheduling, and kernel optimizations are closed-source.

products.description: Proprietary SDK and runtime for running inference on AWS's custom Inferentia2 and Trainium chips. The Neuron Compiler converts models from PyTorch/JAX into optimized executables for AWS custom silicon. Offers significant cost savings vs GPU instances for supported model architectures. Integrated with SageMaker and EC2. AWS's play to break NVIDIA GPU dependency for inference workloads — custom silicon with a proprietary software stack.
products.classification_rationale: Proprietary compiler and runtime that loads model weights and executes inference on custom hardware. The Neuron compiler, runtime, and hardware are all proprietary.

products.product_name: Google Cloud TPU Inference (Pathways / TPU Runtime)
products.description: Proprietary inference runtime for Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), now in v5e/v6e generations. The Pathways system enables efficient model serving across TPU pods with automatic model partitioning. Powers Google's own production inference for Gemini and internal models. Available via Vertex AI and GKE for external customers. The most mature custom-silicon inference stack, developed over 8+ years of TPU generations.
products.classification_rationale: Proprietary hardware and runtime serving model inference. The TPU architecture, XLA backend, and Pathways serving system are closed-source.

products.description: Managed inference service providing a unified API across OpenAI models, open-source models (Llama, Mistral, Phi), and Microsoft's own models. Handles model loading, scaling, and hardware allocation behind a single REST API. Supports serverless (pay-per-token) and provisioned (dedicated capacity) deployments. The enterprise default for organizations on Azure — integrated with Azure AD, networking, and compliance controls.
products.classification_rationale: Managed inference service that loads model weights and serves predictions behind a proprietary API and infrastructure layer. The orchestration, routing, and optimization stack are closed.

products.description: On-device inference runtime that executes models across Apple's heterogeneous compute — CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine — on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Vision Pro. The compiler automatically partitions model graphs across available hardware for optimal latency and power efficiency. Powers Siri, on-device autocorrect, image recognition, and Apple Intelligence features. The most widely deployed on-device inference runtime by install base (2B+ active Apple devices).
products.classification_rationale: Proprietary on-device runtime that loads model weights and runs inference. The Neural Engine hardware, Metal GPU backend, and Core ML runtime are all closed. (coremltools for model conversion is open-source, but the runtime itself is proprietary.)

products.description: Inference service running on custom Reconfigurable Dataflow Architecture (RDA) chips — the SN40L processor with 1TB+ on-chip memory. Designed for large models that don't fit in GPU memory without tensor parallelism. Offers both cloud API and on-premise appliance (DataScale) for enterprise deployments. Competitive with Groq and Cerebras on throughput for large models. Raised $1.5B+, primarily targeting enterprise and government customers.
products.classification_rationale: Custom hardware + proprietary compiler and runtime that loads model weights and serves inference. The chip architecture, dataflow compiler, and serving runtime are all proprietary.

products.description: On-device inference runtime for Qualcomm's Snapdragon processors targeting mobile, automotive, IoT, and PC. Provides unified API across Qualcomm's Hexagon NPU, Adreno GPU, and Kryo CPU with automatic hardware dispatch for optimal performance and power. Powers on-device AI in billions of Android phones and Copilot+ PCs. Supports transformer models with quantization down to INT4. The dominant inference runtime for Android on-device AI workloads.
products.classification_rationale: Proprietary on-device runtime that loads model weights and serves inference on Qualcomm hardware. The NPU architecture, compiler, and runtime are closed-source.

products.description: Meta's open inference + deployment runtime for LLMs — originally launched as Llama Stack (`meta-llama/llama-stack`) in 2024 and rebranded in 2026 as OGX / Open GenAI Stack (`ogx-ai/ogx`) with model-agnostic positioning. Unified APIs for inference, agents, fine-tuning, and eval; 25+ ecosystem partners including AWS, NVIDIA, Databricks, Groq, and Azure. MIT licensed, 8.4K+ stars with continuous commit history across the rename. Anchors the 1B+ Llama downloads ecosystem.
key_dependencies: Pluggable inference backends (vLLM, Ollama, HuggingFace, Together, Fireworks, etc.)
products.classification_rationale: Loads Llama (and other) model weights and serves inference behind an OpenAI-compatible API — the headline behavior is 'serve your model', placing it in Cat 4 per the Cat 4 vs Cat 7 litmus. Agents/eval/fine-tune APIs are auxiliary surfaces, not the primary marketing.

categories.parity_verdict: OSS dominates fine-tuning code — TRL, Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory, Unsloth, PEFT, and verl together cover SFT/LoRA/QLoRA/DPO/RLHF/GRPO at parity or better than any closed offering; closed-source platforms compete on managed convenience and proprietary model access (GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini) rather than capability.
coverage_gaps: Closed-source fine-tuning is structurally thin — most managed offerings are wrappers around OSS techniques applied to proprietary weights
Diffusion/image model fine-tuning tools (Kohya, OneTrainer) are excluded here as we focused on LLM fine-tuning per the Model Code layer scope
Reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) for reasoning models is an emerging sub-segment with limited mature tooling beyond verl and OpenRLHF
categories.thin_segment_note: The closed segment is structurally thin: fine-tuning is mostly an OSS-led discipline because labs that want full control over weights run open frameworks on their own GPUs. Closed offerings are typically managed services from cloud platforms (AWS Bedrock, Vertex, Azure) or model vendors (OpenAI, Cohere, Mistral) — they compete on convenience and proprietary-model access, not on novel training methods. We documented 10 closed entries by including the major model-vendor APIs and the largest cloud hyperscaler offerings; smaller closed startups (Predibase, Lamini, OpenPipe) are included where they have distinct positioning.

products.description: The de facto reference library for post-training transformers — supports SFT, DPO, GRPO, PPO, KTO, reward modeling, and other preference-optimization methods through unified Trainer APIs. Picked over alternatives because it sits at the center of the HF ecosystem (transformers, datasets, accelerate, PEFT) and ships canonical reference implementations that papers and other frameworks build on. 18.4K GitHub stars, 482 contributors, ~400 commits in 90 days — extremely active.
key_dependencies: Optional: PEFT for LoRA, vLLM for online RL rollouts
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: TRL modifies model weights via SFT, DPO, GRPO, PPO trainers — it produces fine-tuned checkpoints, not measurements. Primary function is training, so Finetuning Code (not Eval).

products.description: State-of-the-art Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning library implementing LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA, adapters, prompt tuning, prefix tuning, and IA3 as a drop-in wrapper around transformers models. Picked because it's the underlying adapter engine that TRL, Axolotl, Unsloth, and most other frameworks compose on top of — touching PEFT is unavoidable in the modern fine-tuning stack. 21.2K GitHub stars, 300 contributors, 116 commits in 90 days.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: PEFT wraps base model weights and trains low-rank adapters that modify effective model behavior — it is squarely fine-tuning code, not eval or inference.

products.description: YAML-config-driven fine-tuning framework — wraps TRL, PEFT, DeepSpeed, FSDP, and bitsandbytes behind a single config file so users can run SFT, LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tunes, and DPO across 100+ model families without writing training loops. Picked for serious multi-GPU production fine-tuning where reproducibility via config matters and where Unsloth's single-GPU optimizations don't apply. 12K GitHub stars, 240 contributors, 185 commits in 90 days; the de facto tool for hobbyist and indie fine-tuners shipping models on HF Hub.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Axolotl is a wrapper that orchestrates training runs producing new model weights — its primary function is fine-tuning, not evaluation or inference.

products.description: Unified efficient fine-tuning of 100+ LLMs and VLMs with both CLI and a browser-based Web UI (LlamaBoard) for configuring runs. Picked when teams want a beginner-friendly entry point that's still capable of serious experiments — covers SFT, RLHF, DPO, GRPO, LoRA, QLoRA, freeze, and full fine-tuning. By raw popularity it's the #1 fine-tuning framework on GitHub with 71.5K stars (largely driven by Chinese and global enterprise adoption), 273 contributors, and an ACL 2024 publication backing it.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: LLaMA-Factory's core function is launching training jobs that update model weights via SFT, DPO, PPO, etc. — pure fine-tuning code.

products.description: Performance-optimized fine-tuning library that rewrites kernels in Triton/CUDA to deliver 2-5x faster training with 60-80% less memory on a single GPU — makes 7B/13B LoRA fine-tuning feasible on a consumer RTX 4090. Picked when hardware is constrained and the workload fits one GPU; Unsloth's kernels also slot under TRL trainers so it complements rather than replaces the broader ecosystem. 65K GitHub stars and ~1500 commits in 90 days makes it the fastest-moving repo in the category; widely promoted on r/LocalLLaMA as the default for local fine-tuning.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Unsloth's whole purpose is to accelerate training runs that update model weights — it is fine-tuning code by both function and self-description.

products.description: PyTorch-native post-training library with hand-written, abstraction-free recipes for SFT, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, and PPO across Llama, Gemma, Phi, Mistral, and Qwen. Picked by researchers and PyTorch-first teams who want clean, hackable training code without the framework sprawl of transformers/TRL — recipes tested on 24GB consumer GPUs. 5.8K GitHub stars, 164 contributors; pace slowed recently (only 5 commits in 90 days) as PyTorch focuses post-training investment on TorchTitan/TorchAO, but still actively maintained.
key_dependencies: Optional: bitsandbytes for QLoRA, HF tokenizers
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: torchtune ships training recipes (SFT, LoRA, DPO, PPO) that produce updated model weights — it is fine-tuning code, not evaluation.

products.description: Ray-based distributed RLHF/agentic-RL framework that distributes Actor, Reward, Reference, and Critic models across GPUs for full-scale 70B+ training. Picked over TRL when training scale exceeds a single node and the workload is RL-heavy (PPO, DAPO, REINFORCE++, GRPO, KTO) — combines Ray + vLLM for high-throughput rollouts with DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 for memory-efficient training. 9.5K GitHub stars, 87 contributors, published research backing (arxiv 2405.11143); used by labs scaling preference optimization.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: OpenRLHF runs PPO/DPO/GRPO loops that update actor model weights — RL post-training is squarely fine-tuning code.

products.description: HybridFlow flexible and efficient RL post-training framework developed by ByteDance Seed MLSys and HKU — purpose-built for RLHF and reasoning RL on math and code tasks. Picked when teams need state-of-the-art GRPO/PPO at frontier scale; verl shipped early support for DeepSeek-R1-style reasoning RL recipes and has become a reference implementation in the post-DeepSeek wave. 21.5K GitHub stars, 618 contributors, ~420 commits in 90 days — one of the fastest-growing repos in the category.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: verl orchestrates RL training loops (PPO, GRPO) that update actor weights — fine-tuning code, specifically for reasoning post-training.

products.description: Alibaba ModelScope's unified PEFT/full-parameter CPT/SFT/DPO/GRPO toolkit covering 600+ LLMs and 300+ MLLMs (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1, GLM, Llama4, InternVL, etc.). Picked over LLaMA-Factory when working in the ModelScope ecosystem or when broad multimodal model coverage matters — SWIFT often ships day-zero recipes for Chinese-origin models. 14.2K GitHub stars, 147 contributors, 335 commits in 90 days; published as AAAI 2025.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: SWIFT runs SFT, DPO, GRPO, CPT training jobs that modify model weights — primary function is fine-tuning, not eval.

products.description: 20+ from-scratch implementations of high-performance open LLMs (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Phi, Qwen) with recipes for pretrain, finetune (LoRA, QLoRA, full), and deploy at scale. Picked by teams that want a clean, hackable, single-file-per-model codebase optimized for Lightning Fabric and FSDP, rather than the abstraction layers of transformers/TRL. 13.4K GitHub stars, 132 contributors; pace has slowed (14 commits in 90 days) but the library remains a popular teaching/research baseline.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: LitGPT ships fine-tuning recipes (LoRA/QLoRA/full) that update weights — fine-tuning code, not eval. Pretraining is also supported but post-training is the dominant use.

products.description: NVIDIA's scalable open-source toolkit for RL post-training, successor to NeMo-Aligner — supports DPO, PPO, GRPO, and reward modeling on Megatron-LM and FSDP backends with first-class multi-node H100/B200 scaling. Picked when teams are already on the NVIDIA NeMo stack and need RL post-training that scales to thousands of GPUs. 1.6K GitHub stars but 181 commits in 90 days and a growing contributor base — well-resourced; pairs with NeMo Customizer (managed) for enterprise users.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: NeMo-RL runs RL training loops that update actor weights — fine-tuning code, specifically the alignment/RL slice.

products.description: Managed fine-tuning for GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1, and o-series via the OpenAI API — supports supervised fine-tuning, DPO (added late 2024), and vision fine-tuning. Picked when the use case demands GPT-4-tier quality at lower latency/cost on a narrow task; the only way to fine-tune OpenAI's frontier weights. Training priced at ~$3/M tokens for GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o (GPT-4.1 family ~$0.80-3/M); models served at standard inference rates.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: this API takes a base GPT-4o checkpoint and produces a new fine-tuned variant with updated weights — fine-tuning code (delivered as a service).

artifacts.pricing_model: per-token training fees (~$0.80-$25/M training tokens depending on model) plus inference at standard or 2x rates

products.description: Managed fine-tuning for Anthropic Claude 3 Haiku, Meta Llama, Cohere Command, Amazon Titan, and Amazon Nova models inside Bedrock — the only fully managed service offering fine-tuning of Claude weights. GA since mid-2024; usage requires Provisioned Throughput commitment for inference.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Bedrock fine-tuning produces new model weights (or custom adapters) deployed back through Bedrock — fine-tuning code as a managed service.

artifacts.pricing_model: per-token training plus Provisioned Throughput hourly fees for serving custom models

products.product_name: Vertex AI Tuning (Gemini SFT and Preference Tuning)
products.description: Managed supervised fine-tuning and preference tuning for Gemini 2.0/2.5 Flash and Pro inside Google Cloud Vertex AI — covers text, image, audio, and document tuning with as few as 100 labeled examples. products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Vertex tuning updates Gemini model weights (or LoRA adapters) for the customer — fine-tuning code as a managed service.

artifacts.pricing_model: per-token training fees plus standard Gemini inference rates for the tuned endpoint

products.description: Azure-managed fine-tuning of GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1, and GPT-3.5 with enterprise controls (VNet, private endpoints, RBAC, content filters) that the raw OpenAI API doesn't expose. key_dependencies: Azure subscription with Azure OpenAI access

products.description: Managed fine-tuning across 50+ open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) supporting LoRA, full-parameter SFT, tool-call/reasoning-trace/VLM tuning, and models up to 1T params; resulting checkpoints served at base-model inference rates. Together AI raised $305M Series B at $3.3B valuation (Feb 2025), hit $1B ARR by Feb 2026, with Salesforce, Zoom, and The Washington Post among 450K+ developer accounts.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Together's API ingests data and produces new fine-tuned weights served back through their inference layer — fine-tuning code as a managed service.

products.description: Managed LoRA fine-tuning for popular open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) with served checkpoints at base-model inference rates and tight integration to Fireworks' high-throughput inference engine. Picked when latency-sensitive production serving matters as much as the fine-tune itself — Fireworks consistently benchmarks at the low end of TTFT for hosted open-weight models. Pricing from $0.50/M training tokens for models up to 16B.
key_dependencies: training data via API or Fireworks CLI
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Fireworks' fine-tuning service produces new LoRA adapters that modify base model behavior — fine-tuning code as a managed service.

artifacts.pricing_model: ~$0.50-$16/M training tokens depending on model size; served at base-model inference rates

products.description: Managed LoRA-based supervised fine-tuning of Cohere's Command R model with a 16,384-token training context optimized for RAG and agent workloads. Picked when teams want Cohere's enterprise positioning (data residency, contract terms) and Command R quality on a customized task. Pricing ~$3/M training tokens, then $0.30/M input and $1.20/M output for inference; also available on AWS SageMaker and OCI Generative AI.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Cohere's fine-tuning API produces a new fine-tuned Command R variant with updated weights — fine-tuning code as a service.

artifacts.pricing_model: $3/M training tokens (one-time); served at $0.30/M input + $1.20/M output

products.description: Managed LoRA fine-tuning of Mistral 7B, Mistral Small, and other Mistral models via La Plateforme — plus an open-source companion (mistral-finetune) for self-hosted training. Picked when teams want Mistral's European data residency story or open-weight portability between managed and self-hosted training. API priced at ~$2/M training tokens; the only managed offering for Mistral's commercial weights.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: produces a new fine-tuned Mistral variant served from La Plateforme — fine-tuning code as a managed service.

artifacts.pricing_model: ~$2/M training tokens; served at standard Mistral inference rates

products.description: Managed fine-tuning platform (SFT, continued pretraining, RFT/reinforcement fine-tuning, LoRAX multi-LoRA serving) — pioneered end-to-end RFT and multi-tenant LoRA serving for production inference. Acquired by Rubrik in June 2025 and now operates as the tuning engine inside Rubrik's SAGE / Agent Cloud governance product. Discrete Predibase SKU still available but increasingly absorbed into Rubrik's agentic-AI governance positioning.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Predibase produces fine-tuned LoRA adapters and serves them — fine-tuning code as a service.

artifacts.pricing_model: subscription tiers plus per-hour GPU charges for training and serving
