Acquired by CoreWeave in September 2025 to anchor their RL-for-agents capability alongside Weights & Biases; ART continues active development as the open library, with the platform serving as the commercial wrapper.
key_dependencies: OpenPipe SDK installed in production app
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: OpenPipe ingests logged prompts and produces new fine-tuned open-weight models served back through their API — fine-tuning code as a service. The managed platform is closed source.

products.description: Enterprise fine-tuning stack acquired by AMD at Advancing AI 2025 (June 2025) and rolled into AMD's ROCm/AI software organization; the former CEO Sharon Zhou is now VP of AI at AMD. Picked when teams running on AMD Instinct MI300/MI325 accelerators want a first-party fine-tuning path optimized for ROCm — Lamini's Mixture of Memory Experts (MoME) technique trains thousands of LoRA-style memory experts per model to drive ~95% factual recall with ~10x fewer hallucinations than vanilla SFT. The discrete lamini.ai SaaS has been wound down; the technology now anchors AMD's enterprise fine-tuning story alongside ROCm 6.x and AMD's growing data-center AI revenue ramp.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Lamini's MoME pipeline trains LoRA-style memory experts that update effective model behavior — fine-tuning code, now delivered as an AMD-positioned managed offering rather than a standalone SaaS.

artifacts.pricing_model: bundled with AMD Instinct enterprise engagements; no standalone public SKU since the AMD acquisition

products.description: Ray-based managed fine-tuning platform that wraps LLMForge and ray-llm to run SFT, continued pretraining, LoRA, and preference optimization (DPO, KTO, ORPO, PPO) across Llama-3, Mistral, Mixtral, and other open-weight families — then deploys the resulting checkpoints with LoRA multiplexing on the same cluster. Anyscale raised a $100M Series C at a $1B valuation in 2021 and has reached ~$281M total raised; Ray itself powers training and serving workloads at Uber, Pinterest, Spotify, OpenAI, Cohere, and Instacart, with Anyscale capturing the managed-platform tier above it.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test: Anyscale's LLMForge pipelines run SFT and preference-optimization training that updates model weights and produces deployable checkpoints — fine-tuning code as a managed service. The underlying Ray library is open; the platform itself is closed.

artifacts.pricing_model: consumption-based on Anyscale-managed Ray clusters (per-hour GPU pricing for training and serving)

products.description: Serverless fine-tuning function inside Snowflake Cortex AI for Llama 3 (8B/70B), Llama 3.1 (8B/70B), Mistral 7B, and Mixtral 8x7B — training and inference both run on Snowflake compute without exporting data to a third-party platform. Picked when training data already lives in Snowflake tables and the value of in-perimeter governance (Unity-style RBAC, audit trails, region pinning across AWS US-West-2/US-East-1/EU-Central-1 and Azure East US 2) outweighs catalog breadth. key_dependencies: training data as Snowflake tables or staged files
Cortex AI enabled in a supported region

artifacts.pricing_model: Snowflake credits per million training tokens (see Service Consumption Table); tuned model served at standard AI_COMPLETE token rates with no Provisioned Throughput commitment

products.description: Language-model reinforcement-learning environments framework for collecting and evaluating LLM trajectories across diverse environments. Nous positions it as part of the post-training stack, and the GitHub repo has 1.2K stars, 362 forks, and active 2026 development, which makes it a meaningful open-source training primitive.
products.classification_rationale: It supports RL/post-training workflows rather than serving, chatting, or benchmark-only evaluation.

products.description: Managed training API for researchers that lets teams control the training loop while Thinking Machines handles the infrastructure. It exposes four core primitives — forward_backward, optim_step, sample, and save_state — and supports frontier open-weight models including Qwen, GPT-OSS, Llama, DeepSeek, and Nemotron. Scale signal: Thinking Machines announced a multi-year, gigawatt-scale strategic partnership with NVIDIA and said NVIDIA made a significant investment to support the company’s long-term growth.
products.classification_rationale: Tinker modifies model weights through a managed training workflow, which is the defining Cat 5 litmus test; it is not an inference server, evaluation harness, or chat UI.

categories.parity_verdict: Open-source dominates the eval-harness category — every widely-used benchmark runner (SWE-bench, lm-evaluation-harness, Inspect AI, OpenCompass, Promptfoo, DeepEval) is OSS, with closed offerings mostly differentiating via managed dashboards, proprietary judge models, and private benchmark sets rather than the harness itself.
coverage_gaps: Closed evaluation services often blur into telemetry/observability (Galileo, Patronus, Confident AI) — boundary calls noted in classification_rationale
Many domain-specific eval harnesses (finance, medical, legal) exist but are excluded for breadth — the 10 open entries reflect the most-cited general-purpose harnesses
Benchmark-as-a-service providers like Vals AI and Epoch AI publish leaderboards but run private harnesses; their software is closed and limited public detail exists
OpenAI Evals straddles open/closed — the GitHub repo is MIT-licensed but the OpenAI Dashboard Evals API is a managed commercial product (counted separately)

products.description: Docker-based evaluation harness that benchmarks coding agents on 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 popular Python repositories, producing pass-rate scores against held-out tests. Picked because it is the de-facto industry standard for measuring software-engineering agent capability — every frontier lab (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) reports SWE-bench Verified scores. ~5k stars on GitHub and Epoch AI maintains an authoritative leaderboard. Note: OpenAI's April 2026 audit flagged that 59.4% of the hardest unsolved problems in SWE-bench Verified had flawed test cases — they now prefer the harder SWE-bench Pro and SWE-bench Bash variants for frontier evaluation.
key_dependencies: model API access or local weights
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: this is the harness software that takes a model prediction file, applies the patch in a Docker sandbox, and runs tests to produce a score. The dataset (2,294 issues) ships with it but the primary artifact is the runner, not the data.

products.description: Unified framework for evaluating language models on 200+ academic NLP benchmarks (MMLU, ARC, GSM8K, HellaSwag, etc.) with a single config-driven CLI. Picked as the canonical reference harness — it powers the Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard and is the standard tool for reporting reproducible benchmark numbers in papers. 12.6k GitHub stars, 392 contributors, 58 commits in last 90 days.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: framework for running models against benchmark suites and emitting scores. Ships task definitions but its primary purpose is the scoring loop, not the data itself.

products.description: Evaluation harness for code generation models on 1,140 practical programming tasks requiring use of multiple libraries and tools, scored with branch-coverage tests. Picked over HumanEval because it tests real-world library use rather than self-contained algorithmic puzzles. Hosts the BigCode Models Leaderboard; 500+ GitHub stars on the harness, plus 1k+ stars on the sister bigcode-evaluation-harness for code-completion models.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: per the prompt note, BigCodeBench is kept here as a harness — the repo includes the runner that executes generated code against test cases and computes pass@k, not just a static dataset dump.

products.description: Comprehensive evaluation platform supporting 100+ datasets across Llama, Mistral, GPT-4, Claude, Qwen, GLM and more, with subjective (arena-style) and objective scoring modes. Picked over lm-eval-harness for Chinese-language and multimodal coverage; backed by Shanghai AI Lab and updated weekly. 7k+ GitHub stars, 162 contributors, 25 commits in last 90 days.
key_dependencies: model API access or local weights
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: scores models against benchmark suites and produces leaderboard reports. Multiple datasets ship in-repo but the primary artifact is the evaluation engine.

products.description: Pytest-style evaluation framework for LLM apps with 40+ built-in metrics including G-Eval, hallucination, faithfulness and RAG-specific scores. Picked for CI/CD integration — drops into existing test suites and gates merges on metric thresholds. 15.6k stars, 263 contributors, 561 commits in last 90 days — the most active open-source eval framework on GitHub.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: offline test runner that produces pass/fail and numeric scores per metric. The sister Confident AI cloud platform crosses into telemetry but the DeepEval OSS library is squarely an offline eval harness.

products.description: CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps with declarative YAML configs, side-by-side prompt comparison, and CI/CD gating. Picked for prompt-engineering workflows because of the simple YAML config and built-in red-team/jailbreak scanner. 21.5k stars, 283 contributors, 1,265 commits in last 90 days — used by OpenAI and Anthropic internally per the project README.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: runs prompts against models and grades outputs against assertions (factuality, similarity, regex, LLM-as-judge). Output is offline test reports, not production monitoring.

products.description: Framework for evaluating LLMs and LLM systems plus a registry of community-contributed benchmarks, published as the original 2023 reference implementation for eval-driven development. Picked because it is the canonical starting point referenced in OpenAI's own docs and many derivative harnesses. 18.5k stars but development has effectively slowed (2 commits in last 90 days) as work migrated to the closed OpenAI Dashboard Evals API.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: explicitly described as 'a framework for evaluating LLMs', shipping graders, samplers, and a registry of eval YAML specs. Offline benchmarking, not production monitoring.

products.description: OpenAI's lightweight reference harness used to produce the model cards for GPT-4o, o1, and successors — includes MMLU, MATH, GPQA, MGSM, DROP, HumanEval and SimpleQA. Picked when researchers want the exact numbers OpenAI reports rather than community variants. 4.5k stars, used as the authoritative reproduction script for GPT scorecards.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: small script collection that runs models against fixed benchmark sets and produces the table of scores. Distinct from the larger openai/evals framework.

products.description: Managed evaluation product inside the OpenAI Platform — Evals API plus a Dashboard UI that lets developers define eval datasets, run them against any OpenAI model, grade with custom or built-in graders, and track regressions across versions. Picked by teams already on OpenAI who want the 'measure → improve → ship' loop without standing up infra. Pricing rolls into standard OpenAI API token usage.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: managed offline evaluation runs scored against datasets, with graders and dashboards. Distinct from the open-source openai/evals repo — this is the productized commercial service.

products.description: Evaluation framework purpose-built for Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines with 30+ metrics covering retrieval quality (context precision/recall), generation faithfulness, and answer relevance. Picked when the system under test is RAG — Ragas decomposes pipeline failure into retrieval vs. generation buckets in a way general harnesses do not. 14k stars, 240 contributors.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: scores RAG outputs against ground-truth or synthetic test sets offline. Crosses into observability only via optional Langfuse/LangSmith integrations, but the core library is a harness.

products.description: Frontier-AI evaluation framework with one interface over OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Bedrock and local vLLM/Ollama backends, plus a collection of 200+ pre-built evals (Inspect Evals) co-maintained with Arcadia Impact and the Vector Institute. Picked by AISI, EU AI Office, and many frontier labs as the standard for safety/dangerous-capability evaluations. 2.1k stars but extremely active — 1,333 commits in last 90 days, 227 contributors.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: government-backed harness explicitly built to run benchmarks (including agentic/tool-use evals) against models and produce capability/safety scores. Not a production monitor.

products.description: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models — Python framework for reproducible, transparent evaluation of foundation models including LLMs and multimodal models, organized around scenarios, adapters, and metrics. Picked for academic-grade reproducibility and breadth (accuracy, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity). 2.8k stars, 128 contributors, 151 commits in last 90 days; Stanford has announced HELM will enter maintenance mode June 2026.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: large reproducible benchmark runner that produces leaderboards across many scenarios and metric families. Datasets are referenced but the framework is the artifact.

products.description: Lightweight successor to the eval harness HF used internally — supports vLLM, transformers, TGI and OpenAI-compatible backends with a focus on speed and easy custom metric authoring. Picked when teams want a fast, hackable runner that integrates cleanly with the HF ecosystem (datasets, accelerate). 2.4k stars, 120 contributors, 17 commits in last 90 days; powers parts of the Open LLM Leaderboard v2.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: HF's own benchmark runner, designed for offline scoring across academic suites. Sibling to lm-eval-harness in purpose, distinct in implementation.

products.description: Scalable, real-computer environment for benchmarking multimodal agents on 369 open-ended tasks across Ubuntu, Windows and macOS — agents drive a virtual desktop and are scored by execution-based test scripts. Picked because it is the leading harness for computer-use agents (Claude Computer Use, OpenAI Operator both publish OSWorld scores). 2.9k stars, 86 contributors, 55 commits in last 90 days.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: harness that spins up VMs, lets an agent take actions, then runs test scripts to grade success. Both data (369 tasks) and runner ship together but the primary artifact is the execution-and-scoring infrastructure.

products.description: Crowd-sourced pairwise model comparison platform where users chat with two anonymous models and vote for the better response, producing Bradley-Terry Elo rankings over 200+ models. Picked as the most-cited human-preference benchmark in the field — every frontier lab announces its 'Arena rank' on release. Rebranded from LMArena to Arena in January 2026; raised $100M seed (2025) + $150M Series A at $1.7B valuation (January 2026, a16z lead). Over 6.3M votes collected as of early 2026.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: the Arena software is a managed evaluation system that scores models via head-to-head matchups and produces a leaderboard. The voting platform and Elo pipeline are closed; the live ranking service that frontier labs cite is the commercial product (FastChat, the historical OSS chat backend, is separate).

products.description: Managed evaluation platform built around proprietary judge models — Lynx (8B hallucination detector), GLIDER (3.8B explainable rubric judge) and Percival (agent execution-trace analyzer). Picked by enterprises needing managed eval models rather than spinning up their own LLM-as-judge. Raised $20M; usage-based pricing $10-$20 per 1,000 evaluator API calls.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: primary product is running test suites of inputs/outputs through proprietary scorer models and returning numeric grades — offline batch evaluation. Percival adds trace-style analysis but the platform is positioned around pre-deploy evaluation, not live production monitoring (which would push it toward Telemetry).

products.description: Enterprise evaluation and red-teaming service combining expert human raters, in-house prompt engineers, and proprietary benchmark suites for frontier-model developers and enterprises. Picked because Scale is the third-party evaluator for the US AI Safety Institute and runs custom evals for major labs that cannot be reproduced with OSS tools. March 2026 launch of Scale Labs (expansion of the 2023 SEAL division) consolidates this offering.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: service runs offline benchmark and red-team evaluations against a target model and delivers reports. Not production monitoring of live traffic.

products.description: Independent benchmarking service that runs 10+ academic and agentic evals (MMLU, GPQA, long-context, etc.) against every major model and publishes the Intelligence Index — a composite score with 95% CIs. Picked as the go-to neutral leaderboard for model selection: their Index v3 score is widely cited and covers 300+ models across 100+ providers. Raised a seed round via the Nat Friedman / Daniel Gross AIGrant program.

products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: the company's primary product is running benchmark suites against models and publishing scores. The harness is proprietary even though it consumes some open datasets; their differentiator is the index methodology and confidence intervals.

artifacts.pricing_model: free leaderboard; paid API/data feed for enterprise

products.description: Domain-specialist benchmarking service that runs proprietary, held-out evals over finance, law, software, and healthcare tasks — including a private Canadian-court-case QA benchmark and the Vals Index. Picked by enterprises that need closed/private benchmarks because public benchmarks suffer from contamination. Publishes a leaderboard of all major frontier models scored on these private sets.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: software that runs models against private, domain-specific benchmark suites and publishes scores. Closed-source harness with closed-source datasets — the differentiator vs OSS is exactly the privacy and contamination resistance.

artifacts.pricing_model: enterprise contract; public leaderboard free to view

products.description: Independent benchmarking lab that runs and maintains canonical leaderboards for high-stakes evals (SWE-bench Verified, FrontierMath, GPQA Diamond) and operates the FrontierMath private math benchmark. Picked when researchers want the authoritative scoreboard for a specific benchmark — Epoch's SWE-bench Verified leaderboard is the one frontier labs reference in announcements. Funded by Open Philanthropy and lab partners.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: software/service that runs models against benchmark suites (some private, like FrontierMath) and publishes scores. The harness is internal even though some underlying datasets are public.

products.description: Managed evaluation service inside Amazon Bedrock for scoring foundation models and RAG systems with three modes: automatic (BERTScore, F1, accuracy, robustness, toxicity), LLM-as-a-Judge (correctness, completeness, harmfulness, custom prompts), and human evaluation (internal workforce or AWS-managed reviewer team). Differentiates by being native to the Bedrock model catalog and Knowledge Bases — eval jobs run against any Bedrock-supported model, results tie directly into the model deployment pipeline, and comparative analysis across runs is built in. Bedrock model evaluation went GA April 2024; the LLM-as-a-Judge variant went GA March 2025. Bedrock as a platform serves tens of thousands of customers (per AWS, Dec 2024) including adidas, Intuit, Pfizer, Salesforce, Siemens, Thomson Reuters, and the NYSE.
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: runs offline batch evaluation jobs against datasets to produce numeric scores and human-rated reports for model selection and pre-deployment quality gating — not production-traffic telemetry (which would push it to Cat 9). Distinct from Bedrock fine-tuning (Cat 5) since no weights are modified.

artifacts.pricing_model: per-inference token usage for judge and target models (no separate evaluations surcharge); human-evaluation workforce billed separately for AWS-managed reviewers

products.description: Managed evaluation service on Vertex AI (now part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) that scores generative-AI outputs using three approaches: computation-based metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, exact match), LLM-as-judge with Gemini as the judge model (including adaptive rubrics that auto-generate per-prompt pass/fail tests), and AutoSxS pairwise pipelines that A/B test two models with a judge declaring a winner. Differentiates on tight integration with Vertex AI pipelines, Model Garden, Gemini tuning workflows, and LiteLLM for third-party models — eval datasets can be built from production logs or synthetic data and run across seven global regions. Used by Vertex AI customers including Wendy's, Wayfair, Verizon, Mercedes-Benz, and Etsy (per Google Cloud case studies) as the canonical eval surface for Gemini-based applications.
key_dependencies: GCP project with Vertex AI enabled
Gemini or third-party model access (via LiteLLM)
products.classification_rationale: Eval Code: offline scoring service that runs evaluation datasets against models and emits metric reports, pairwise winners, and rubric verdicts. Not production telemetry — Vertex AI Model Monitoring is the separate Cat 9 surface for live-traffic monitoring.

artifacts.pricing_model: per-token charges for judge-model inference plus standard Vertex AI pipeline/compute fees (no separate eval-service line item)

categories.thin_segment_note: After moving Galileo and Confident AI Cloud to Telemetry Observability and Vellum to Orchestration Agents (all three pivoted away from pure eval positioning in 2025-26), the closed segment shrinks. Patronus, Scale Evaluation, OpenAI Evals API, Artificial Analysis, Vals AI, and Epoch AI Benchmarks remain — fewer than 10 because the line between eval and telemetry has collapsed in the market: most modern eval vendors now sell unified eval-plus-observability platforms (counted under Cat 9). Pure offline harness vendors are predominantly open-source.

categories.parity_verdict: Open-source owns the primitives — Firecracker, gVisor, Kata Containers underlie nearly every closed sandbox. But the managed-sandbox-for-agents experience is led by closed offerings (Modal $4.65B valuation, Replit $9B, Vercel Sandboxes, Cloudflare Workers) that out-scale open-core options like E2B and Daytona on UX, observability, and reliability — and the gap is widening, not narrowing.
coverage_gaps: Self-hosted Kubernetes-native sandbox stacks (KEDA, Knative eventing) are under-represented relative to their production footprint
Hyperscaler offerings beyond AWS/GCP (Azure Container Apps, Oracle Functions) omitted to keep the closed list at 10
WASM-based execution runtimes (Wasmer, wasmtime, Spin) excluded — they are primitives more than agent-facing sandbox products
Browser-based sandboxes (CodeSandbox CDE) excluded as they lean IDE rather than agent execution

products.description: Open-source secure cloud runtime that gives AI agents an ephemeral Linux microVM (Firecracker-based) controlled via a Python/TypeScript SDK. Picked over hyperscaler functions for sub-150ms cold starts, agent-native lifecycle (create/use/destroy), and the fact that the SDK + core are open and self-hostable via the e2b-dev/infra repo. ~12.3k stars on the SDK repo, used by major coding-agent products and growing fast in the agent-infra category.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — E2B's whole pitch is letting an agent safely run code (Python scripts, shell commands, tool calls) it generated. No model weights served; just isolated arbitrary code execution.

products.description: Open-source agent-native compute platform that provisions sub-200ms stateful sandboxes (start, pause, fork, snapshot, destroy) for AI agents. Picked over E2B for snapshot/fork semantics and an enterprise BYOC story. Raised $24M Series A in Feb 2026 led by FirstMark with strategic investment from Datadog and Figma Ventures, ~72k stars on GitHub.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Daytona explicitly markets itself as giving every agent a computer for running generated code, shell commands, and tool calls. Not a model server.

products.description: Open-source virtual machine monitor that uses KVM to launch microVMs in milliseconds with a minimal device model. Picked because it is the actual primitive underneath nearly every modern sandbox product (E2B, Vercel Sandbox, Fly Sprites, Koyeb, even AWS Lambda and Fargate). ~34.5k stars and 248 contributors; remains the gold standard for hardware-isolated short-lived compute.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Firecracker exists explicitly to run untrusted arbitrary code (functions, containers, agent sandboxes) in hardware-isolated microVMs. The entire Lambda/sandbox industry sits on top of it.

products.description: Application-kernel sandbox written in Go that intercepts syscalls from a container and serves them in userspace, providing strong isolation without the cost of a full VM. Picked over raw containers when you need defense-in-depth for untrusted code (the exact agent-sandbox use case). Used by Google Cloud Run, Anthropic's compute backend, and Northflank; ~18.4k stars.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — gVisor's reason to exist is sandboxing arbitrary code (containers running anything a user supplied) at the syscall layer. Not a model runtime.

products.description: Open-source runtime that launches each container inside a lightweight VM (QEMU/Cloud Hypervisor/Firecracker) so containers get VM-level isolation with the container UX. Picked when you need OCI-image compatibility plus stronger isolation than runc — used by Northflank's microVM tier and several cloud providers. ~7.9k stars, very active dev (1,121 commits in last 90d).
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Kata exists to safely run arbitrary container workloads (any code a user or agent ships in an OCI image) under hardware isolation. Not a model server.

products.description: Open-source Docker-based sandbox runtime positioned as a self-hostable E2B alternative, with first-class GPU support, Python and Node.js runtimes, and no session time limits. Picked when teams need to keep agent execution on their own infra (HIPAA/SOC2/BYOC) and want GPU workloads alongside CPU sandboxes. ~1.6k stars, AGPL-3.0 licensed with a managed cloud offering.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Beta9 runs arbitrary user/agent code in isolated containers. GPU support is for arbitrary code that happens to need a GPU, not for hosting model weights as a service.

products.description: Apache-2.0 sandbox runtime from Alibaba aimed squarely at AI agents — defines a 'Sandbox Protocol' with standard lifecycle/execution APIs and ships multi-language SDKs (Python, Java, JS, .NET) plus Docker and Kubernetes runtimes. Picked by teams wanting an open protocol-driven alternative to E2B at K8s scale; ~10.8k stars and 910 commits in the last 90d signal serious investment.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — OpenSandbox markets itself as a secure runtime for AI agents to execute generated code, coding-agent workloads, and GUI/RL training. Code in, not weights in.

products.description: Apache-2.0 all-in-one Docker sandbox bundling Browser, Shell, File, MCP server, and VSCode Server in a single container so an agent gets a complete computer-use environment from one image. Picked over E2B/Daytona by builders who want browser+shell+files in one box for computer-use agents rather than wiring up multiple services. ~4.8k stars, actively maintained.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — provides the execution surface for an agent to run shell commands, browse, and edit files. The included VSCode/MCP pieces are tools for the executing agent, not a model-serving system.

products.description: Open-source lightweight sandboxing tool from Anthropic that enforces filesystem and network restrictions on arbitrary processes at the OS level (Linux bubblewrap, macOS seatbelt) without requiring a container. Picked because it powers the bash tool sandbox inside Claude Code and is the reference design for safe local agent execution. ~4.1k stars and active development (63 commits in 90d).
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — purpose-built to safely run shell commands and processes an agent (Claude Code) generated, restricting filesystem and network at the OS layer. Zero involvement in model inference.

products.description: Open-source platform for provisioning remote dev environments (Terraform-defined workspaces on K8s, VMs, or bare metal) — increasingly used as the substrate for self-hosted agent execution environments. Picked over GitHub Codespaces when teams want full BYOC control and have aggressively repositioned in 2026 toward AI-agent workspaces. ~13.3k stars, very active (2,055 commits in 90d).
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Coder workspaces exist to run arbitrary developer/agent code in isolated remote environments. The AI-agent positioning is explicitly about giving an agent its own sandboxed computer.

products.description: The original at-scale serverless function platform — pay-per-invocation execution of arbitrary code in managed Firecracker microVMs with 1M free requests/month free tier. Picked when teams want zero-ops compute that integrates deeply with the rest of AWS; remains the default closed-source compute primitive for event-driven workloads. Closed product running atop the open Firecracker microVM.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Lambda runs arbitrary user code (Python/Node/Go/Java/etc.) in sandboxed microVMs. It's the canonical closed-source counterpart to E2B/Modal, not a model server.

products.description: Closed-source serverless platform that lets you run Python and shell code (including GPU workloads) in seconds-startup containers, with a dedicated Sandbox primitive for executing untrusted agent-generated code. Picked when AI teams need GPU-capable sandboxes with Pythonic ergonomics. Raised $355M Series C in May 2026 at a $4.65B valuation; $300M annualized revenue driven largely by coding-agent demand.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Modal Sandboxes are explicitly the 'safely run code an agent generated' product. Modal also serves inference, but the Sandbox primitive itself is arbitrary-code execution.

products.description: Closed-source compute primitive (GA in 2026) that runs untrusted/agent-generated code in isolated Firecracker microVMs with millisecond startup, default Node 24 + Python 3.13 runtimes, filesystem and shell access. Picked by teams already on Vercel building AI agents that need a managed sandbox tightly integrated with the AI SDK. The execution layer behind Vercel Open Agents.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Vercel's docs explicitly position Sandbox as the layer for safely executing AI-generated code, user uploads, and third-party scripts. Distinct from Vercel's model APIs.

products.description: Cloudflare's two-tier sandboxing for AI agents, shipped during Agents Week 2026: Dynamic Workers (V8 isolates, ms-scale cold start, ~100x faster and more memory-efficient than containers, open beta April 2026) and Sandboxes (persistent Linux environments, GA April 2026 for full-OS workloads). Picked when latency, edge distribution, and isolation density matter; distributed across Cloudflare's global edge network and available to all paid Workers users — the company's headline agent infrastructure release of 2026.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Dynamic Workers exist to let an agent run code it generated inside a per-request isolate. Cloudflare's separate Workers AI product handles model inference; this is the code-execution counterpart.

products.description: Fully managed serverless container platform with gVisor-based sandboxing, pay-per-request pricing, and scale-to-zero. Picked over Lambda for any-OCI-image flexibility and longer max execution. In 2026 Cloud Run added 'Cloud Run Instances' for long-running background agents and deep Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform integration, making it Google's go-to closed-source sandbox for agent code.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Cloud Run runs arbitrary container code, and Google's 2026 messaging positions it as the deployment target for AI agents to execute code. Inference is a separate Vertex AI product.

products.description: Closed-source stateful sandbox product (launched Jan 2026) — Firecracker microVMs with 100GB persistent NVMe storage that boot in 1–12s cold, ~300ms warm checkpoint/restore, and auto-idle when inactive. Picked by teams who reject ephemeral sandboxes for coding agents and want a persistent computer the agent can return to. Pitched explicitly against E2B/Modal/Daytona for long-running Claude Code-style sessions.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — a Sprite is a hardware-isolated execution environment for arbitrary code: a persistent Linux computer for an agent. Not a model server.

products.description: Closed-source cloud dev platform with Nix-based environments supporting 30,000+ OS packages, exposing a Code Execution API that runs untrusted/AI-generated code in sandboxed VMs. Picked when teams want a tightly integrated build+run+deploy story (Replit Agent 4 leans heavily on this) rather than an unbundled SDK. Raised $400M Series D in March 2026 at a $9B valuation; 50M+ users.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Replit's Code Execution API is explicitly designed to safely run code that an AI agent (Replit Agent or external) generated. Replit ships LLM features but the execution sandbox itself is arbitrary code.

products.description: WebAssembly Node.js runtime that boots a full dev environment — filesystem, package manager, terminal, dev server — inside the browser with no remote VM. Picked when an agent and user need to share an in-browser sandbox with millisecond startup and near-zero server cost. `webcontainer-core` is MIT (~4.6K stars) but stale (last push April 2025); the production WebContainer API and StackBlitz/Bolt.new platform are proprietary. Powers Bolt.new, which hit 7M+ users and $40M ARR by Dec 2025; StackBlitz raised Series B in Jan 2025 at $700M valuation.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — WebContainers safely run Node code an agent generated (Bolt.new is the canonical example) inside the user's browser. webcontainer-core repo is MIT but the runtime API is proprietary and license-gated, so we mark the product closed.

products.description: Closed-source code-execution tool exposed via the Responses API and Assistants API — runs Python (and bash in newer versions) in a fully sandboxed VM with attached files, so the model can compute, analyze data, and iterate on solutions. Picked when teams want a turnkey 'agent can run code' primitive bundled directly with the OpenAI model API rather than wiring up E2B/Modal themselves.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Code Interpreter exists to run Python/bash code (not weights) that the model generated, in an isolated sandbox. The model inference is a separate concern; this entry is the execution layer.

products.description: Closed-source managed sandbox platform offering microVM isolation via Kata Containers and gVisor, any OCI image, unlimited session duration, and BYOC deployment. Picked when teams need production-grade isolation plus a complete platform (services, jobs, databases) beyond ephemeral sandboxes; processes 2M+ isolated workloads/month and is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant.
products.classification_rationale: Litmus test passes — Northflank Sandboxes run arbitrary OCI-image workloads (any code, any language) under microVM isolation for agent use cases. Not a model server.

products.description: Managed sandbox platform for hosting interactive ML apps — supports Gradio, Streamlit, Docker, and static SDKs with a free CPU tier, paid CPU/GPU upgrades, and a ZeroGPU shared-pool tier. Differentiates through tight integration with the Hugging Face Hub (one-click deploy from any model card) and community discoverability, making it the default demo surface for nearly every open-weight model release. ~400K+ apps as of early 2026 with reportedly ~40K new Spaces created per month and 100M+ monthly visits; the canonical 'where you go to try an open model in your browser'.
key_dependencies: Gradio (OSS) / Streamlit (OSS) / Docker for app SDKs
Proprietary Spaces runtime and GPU scheduling
products.classification_rationale: Cat 7 litmus 'what goes in the container — model weights or user code?' returns user code — Gradio/Streamlit/Docker apps that the user wrote. Hugging Face's separate Inference Endpoints product handles model serving (Cat 4); Spaces is the arbitrary-code execution layer. Marked is_open 'partial' because Gradio and the Docker pathway are OSS but the Spaces runtime, ZeroGPU scheduling, and managed infra are proprietary — classic open-frontend + closed-platform pattern.

categories.parity_verdict: Open-source has reached genuine parity in the self-hosted chat-UI segment (Open WebUI, LibreChat, Lobe Chat, AnythingLLM rival ChatGPT's UX) and dominates the API-gateway tier (LiteLLM, Helicone), but closed players still own the mass-market consumer surface — ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Grok command billions of users that no open frontend approaches.
coverage_gaps: Vertical/role-specific chat UIs (legal, medical) are under-represented on both sides
Mobile-first open-source chat apps remain weak — most OSS projects assume desktop or self-hosted web
Closed API-gateway/routing layer is thin (OpenRouter is the only meaningful closed-source aggregator at scale; Helicone has both OSS + closed)
Voice-first conversational interfaces (ChatGPT Voice, Gemini Live) have no strong open analogue yet

products.description: Self-hosted, extensible web UI for chatting with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or local Ollama model, with built-in RAG, multimodal support, and a tools/plugins marketplace. Picked over alternatives for its breadth of features (knowledge bases, web search, document chat) and very active development; the most popular open chat frontend with ~138k GitHub stars and 280M+ container pulls by May 2026.
key_dependencies: Requires an LLM endpoint — Ollama, OpenAI API, or any OpenAI-compatible server
products.classification_rationale: Human-driven chat interface: user types prompts, model responds. No autonomous goal pursuit — agentic features are opt-in tool calls inside a human-led session. UI & API, not Orchestration.

products.description: Open-source ChatGPT clone with native support for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, and local model backends, plus multi-user auth, agents, code interpreter, and prompt sharing. Differentiator is enterprise-grade auth/RBAC and the closest faithful clone of ChatGPT's UX, making it popular for org-wide self-hosted deployments; ~37k GitHub stars by mid-2026.
key_dependencies: Requires MongoDB and at least one LLM provider API key or local endpoint
products.classification_rationale: User-facing multi-provider chat interface; agents are tool-augmented chat turns, not autonomous task executors. Human in the driver's seat.

products.description: Python SDK and proxy server (AI gateway) that exposes a single OpenAI-format API across 100+ LLM providers (Bedrock, Azure, Vertex, Anthropic, Cohere, vLLM, etc.) with cost tracking, fallback routing, virtual keys, and guardrails. Picked as the de facto open API gateway for organizations that need provider-agnostic LLM access with spend controls; ~48k GitHub stars and adopted as enterprise gateway by many AI platform teams.
key_dependencies: Provider API credentials for each backend model
products.classification_rationale: Pure API routing/aggregation layer — translates one call format to many. Doesn't make decisions or pursue goals, just relays requests. Classic UI & API per the boundary rules.

products.description: Modern-design open-source chat framework supporting OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Ollama, Azure, DeepSeek and others, with knowledge bases, vision/TTS, plugin marketplace, and one-click deployment. Chosen for its polished UI and breadth of multi-modal/plugin support compared to barebones alternatives; ~77k GitHub stars makes it the second-most-starred OSS chat UI.
key_dependencies: At least one LLM provider API key or local model endpoint
products.classification_rationale: Chat-first UI with plugins invoked inside human-led conversations. No autonomous multi-step task execution as the headline feature.

products.description: All-in-one desktop and Docker app for private, on-device chat with documents (RAG), agents, and 30+ LLM providers including local Ollama. Differentiator is zero-config desktop setup with bundled embedder and vector DB, plus team/Docker mode with RBAC and embeddable widgets; ~60k GitHub stars.
key_dependencies: Optional cloud LLM API keys; ships with bundled local LLM/embedder/LanceDB for desktop
products.classification_rationale: Document-chat product where the user asks questions and reads answers. Agent flow builder exists but it is a configurable tool, not the headline behavior — primary use is human-led RAG chat.

products.description: Lightweight, cross-platform ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude web client that runs as a single Next.js app deployable to Vercel in one click. Picked for its minimalism and easy personal deployment when full-fat frontends like Open WebUI are overkill; ~88k GitHub stars makes it the single most-starred OSS chat UI repo by raw count.
key_dependencies: Provider API key (OpenAI / Anthropic / Google / etc.)
products.classification_rationale: Stateless chat client — user prompts, model responds. No autonomous behavior.

products.description: Open-source chat UI that powers HuggingChat (huggingface.co/chat), giving free public access to open-weights models like Llama, Mistral, Command R+ and others. Differentiator is being the reference SvelteKit chat UI shipped and maintained by Hugging Face itself, with first-class support for TGI/transformers endpoints; ~11k GitHub stars but powers a high-traffic free consumer endpoint.
key_dependencies: MongoDB; an inference endpoint (TGI / transformers / OpenAI-compatible)
products.classification_rationale: Plain chat UI shipped by HF — user prompts, model responds, tools optionally invoked inside the turn. Human-led.

products.description: Cross-platform desktop app (Windows/macOS/Linux) for running open-source models 100% offline, with a clean ChatGPT-style UI, optional cloud provider integrations, and a local OpenAI-compatible API server on localhost:1337. Picked over alternatives for its polished native desktop experience and offline-first stance; 5.3M+ downloads and ~43k GitHub stars by May 2026.
key_dependencies: GGUF models from HuggingFace (bundled downloader); optional remote provider keys
products.classification_rationale: Desktop chat client — UI for human-driven conversations. MCP/tools are opt-in inside chat sessions, not autonomous task execution.

products.description: Open-source AI code assistant for VS Code and JetBrains IDEs offering inline completions, chat, and edit modes against any model (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, vLLM). Differentiates from Copilot by being model-agnostic and self-hostable, and from Cursor by living inside existing IDEs; YC-backed with ~$5M seed and ~33k GitHub stars.
key_dependencies: VS Code or JetBrains IDE; user-supplied LLM endpoint
products.classification_rationale: Code-completion + chat-in-editor where the developer accepts/rejects suggestions turn by turn. The headline feature is human-driven autocomplete and chat, not autonomous task execution — per the spec, this is UI & API.

products.description: Self-hosted chat frontend originally forked from TavernAI, focused on character/roleplay use cases with deep support for prompt engineering, lorebooks, group chats, and any OpenAI-compatible or local backend. Dominant frontend in the open roleplay/character-chat community (~28k GitHub stars) and the de facto UI for users moving off Character.ai to local models.
key_dependencies: A backend (KoboldAI, llama.cpp, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
products.classification_rationale: Pure chat interface — the user drives a roleplay conversation. No autonomous agent loop; it's a UI on top of an inference backend.

products.description: OpenAI's flagship consumer chat product — web, desktop, and mobile apps for conversing with GPT-5/o-series models, with built-in tools (search, code interpreter, image gen, voice, memory). The category-defining UI by a wide margin: 900M weekly active users and 50M paying subscribers as of Feb 2026, on a $25B annualized run rate.
products.classification_rationale: Consumer chat app where the human types prompts and reads answers. Tool use happens inside a turn; agentic modes (ChatGPT Agent) are opt-in features inside the chat UI, not the default behavior. UI & API.

products.description: AI pair-programmer integrated into VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim, and Visual Studio, offering inline code completion, chat, and code review against multiple model backends (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google). Differentiator is enterprise distribution via GitHub and tight IDE integration; ~4.7M paid subscribers and ~$1B ARR as of early 2026.
products.classification_rationale: Per spec edge case: Copilot itself is human-driven completion + chat (you type, you accept/reject suggestions). The agent mode (Copilot Workspace) leans Orchestration but the headline product is UI & API.

products.description: Anthropic's consumer chat product (web, desktop, mobile) for interacting with Claude Sonnet/Opus models, with Projects, Artifacts (live-rendered code/docs), and Computer Use. ~30M monthly active users and adding 1M+ daily signups as of March 2026, third-largest US mobile chatbot.
products.classification_rationale: Consumer chat UI — user drives conversation, models respond. Artifacts and Projects are presentation/organization features, not autonomous agents.

products.description: Google's consumer Gemini chat app on web, Android, iOS, and integrated across Google Workspace, with Live (voice), Deep Research, and image/video generation. 900M+ monthly active users by Q1 2026 (up from 750M at end of 2025), fastest-growing standalone LLM in absolute terms.
products.classification_rationale: Consumer chat surface for Gemini models — human prompts, model responds, optional tool/search. Spark/agent features are opt-in surfaces inside the same chat app.

products.description: Microsoft's consumer/enterprise Copilot chat surface on Windows, web, mobile, and embedded across Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook). 15M paid M365 Copilot seats and 33M active users as of Q2 FY2026, though usage share has slipped vs ChatGPT and Gemini.
key_dependencies: Microsoft account; M365 license for full features
products.classification_rationale: Productivity chat assistant embedded in apps — user drives, AI suggests/generates inside a document or chat. UI & API.

products.description: Search-grounded consumer chat product that returns cited answers with live web results, available on web, mobile, and as a Comet browser. 45M+ MAU and ~$200M ARR with a $21B valuation in 2026; the consumer surface (perplexity.ai) is human-driven Q&A, distinct from the Perplexity API (Cat 11) and the agentic Comet browser.
key_dependencies: Perplexity account; backend models from OpenAI/Anthropic/Meta/in-house Sonar
products.classification_rationale: User asks a question, Perplexity searches and synthesizes a cited answer in one turn. Human-led search-chat, not autonomous goal pursuit. Note: the Perplexity API itself is catalogued under Agent Tools (Cat 11) — this is the consumer chat product only.

products.description: Multi-model chat aggregator letting users talk to GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3 Pro, image/video generators, and 1M+ user-created bots from one interface, with a points-based unified pricing model. Differentiator is breadth (200+ models in one app) plus a creator economy of custom bots; recently added 200-person group chats. Run by Quora.
products.classification_rationale: Multi-model chat front-end and bot marketplace — humans drive conversations, optionally switching models mid-thread. API routing + UI, not autonomous agent.

products.description: Commercial API gateway that exposes 400+ models from 60+ providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, plus open-weights hosts) behind a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint with automatic failover and unified billing. The dominant closed-source LLM aggregator: ~$50M annualized revenue and reportedly raising $120M at a $1.3B valuation (CapitalG-led) in early 2026.
key_dependencies: OpenRouter account credits or BYOK provider keys
products.classification_rationale: API routing/aggregation layer — translates one call to many providers with smart routing. Explicitly listed in the spec as belonging in UI & API.

products.description: Consumer chat product centered on user-created character personas, dialogue roleplay, and conversational entertainment. ~20M MAU and ~6M daily visitors with two hours/day average engagement — one of the stickiest consumer AI surfaces; founders' team was acqui-hired by Google in 2024 but the product continues to operate.
products.classification_rationale: Roleplay/companion chat — user converses with a character. The AI responds in persona but doesn't pursue goals autonomously. Pure UI on top of conversational models.

products.description: xAI's consumer chat product with a standalone app (grok.com) plus deep integration into X (Twitter), competing on real-time data access and a less-filtered tone. ~64M MAU by early 2026 and ~17.8% US chatbot share — third behind ChatGPT and Gemini, with the fastest single-year share gain of any consumer chatbot.
products.classification_rationale: Consumer chat UI on top of Grok models — human in the driver's seat. UI & API, not Orchestration.

products.description: Mistral's consumer/enterprise chat product (chat.mistral.ai) running on Mistral Medium/Large with Flash Answers, web search, image gen, and an enterprise on-prem deployment option. 1M downloads in 14 days at app launch; ~10.8M monthly desktop visits in March 2026 with 21% MoM growth — Europe's flagship sovereign-AI chat surface.
products.classification_rationale: Consumer/enterprise chat UI; Work Mode adds tool use inside the chat but it is a feature toggle, not an autonomous agent.

products.description: Chinese consumer chat app from DeepSeek (Hangzhou) on chat.deepseek.com plus iOS/Android apps, exposing DeepSeek V3/R1 models with thinking mode and web search. ~131.5M MAU in January 2026 (90% MoM surge), second only to ChatGPT in global AI DAU rankings — driven by free access to frontier-tier models.
products.classification_rationale: Consumer chat product — human prompts, model responds with optional reasoning/search. UI surface on DeepSeek's API.

products.description: Meta's consumer AI assistant — a chat surface embedded directly into WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, and Messenger, plus a standalone web app at meta.ai and native iOS/Android apps. Powered by Llama 4/5 across most surfaces with Muse Spark (Meta Superintelligence Labs' new closed-weight model, launched April 8, 2026) backing the standalone app and rolling out to Family-of-Apps in mid-2026. 1B+ monthly active users across Meta's apps — the only consumer AI assistant with native distribution into ~4B existing users; the standalone Meta AI iPhone app has held a top-of-chart App Store position alongside ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini since the Muse Spark launch.
products.classification_rationale: Consumer chat product where the user types and reads — Cat 8 per the standard 'who is in the driver's seat' litmus. The product surface (UX, distribution, app) is proprietary regardless of which backing model is open or closed.

products.description: ByteDance's consumer AI chat app (doubao.com plus iOS/Android) powered by the Doubao Seed model family, with native multimodal support (text, image, audio, video) and a full-duplex real-time voice mode that streams ASR, reasoning, and TTS concurrently for natural barge-in conversation. The largest Chinese consumer AI chat product by daily usage: ~100M DAU baseline with a peak of ~145M DAU during the February 2026 Lunar New Year, ~345M MAU per QuestMobile Q1 2026 (other trackers put it at 220-226M MAU around the same period). Served 1.9B+ queries as the exclusive AI partner of the 2026 CCTV Spring Festival Gala.
products.classification_rationale: Consumer chat UI — human types or speaks, model responds. Voice mode and multimodal generation are features inside human-led turns, not autonomous goal pursuit. Cat 8, not Cat 1.

products.description: Enterprise AI coworker that grounds answers, drafts, slides, voice notes, and task execution in company context across apps and permissions. Glean positions it as the front-door work AI layer for employees, with product screenshots and messaging focused on proactive answers, content generation, and action-taking; the company also has a public $7.2B valuation headline and Gartner/G2 recognition, which signals meaningful enterprise adoption.
products.classification_rationale: This is a human-driven assistant surface: the user prompts it, reviews output, and may optionally ask it to take action, which is Cat 8 rather than Cat 1.

products.description: AI-powered workplace search across 100+ enterprise tools with permissions-aware results, knowledge-graph personalization, and generative answers. Glean’s own product pages and homepage emphasize that it searches everywhere employees work, then turns that context into concise answers and next steps; the company highlights a 141% ROI claim in its Forrester materials as an adoption signal.
products.classification_rationale: This is a human query/search workflow, not an autonomous agent runtime, so it fits the Cat 8 UI/API bucket.

categories.parity_verdict: Competitive — open-source tools (Langfuse, Phoenix, Opik) offer full-featured tracing, cost tracking, and prompt analytics on par with closed alternatives. LangSmith leads on LangChain ecosystem lock-in and Datadog on enterprise APM integration, but OSS options are self-hostable and increasingly the default for startups.
coverage_gaps: Enterprise-specific LLM monitoring bundled into existing APM suites (Splunk, Elastic) may be undercounted
Emerging agent-specific observability tools (multi-agent tracing, tool-call debugging) are a fast-moving sub-segment

products.description: Open-source LLM engineering platform providing tracing, prompt management, evaluations, cost tracking, and datasets. Self-hostable or cloud-hosted. The leading open-source LLM observability platform with broad integrations (OpenTelemetry, LangChain, OpenAI SDK, LiteLLM). YC W23, 27.7K GitHub stars.
key_dependencies: Requires an LLM-powered application to instrument
products.classification_rationale: Primary function is observing, logging, and analyzing LLM system behavior in production — traces, cost tracking, prompt analytics → Telemetry Observability

products.description: Open-source AI observability and evaluation toolkit by Arize AI. Provides tracing, embeddings analysis, experiment tracking, and LLM evaluation in a local-first workflow. Strong integrations with LlamaIndex and LangChain. Built by the team behind the Arize production ML monitoring platform. 9.8K GitHub stars.
key_dependencies: Requires an LLM-powered application to instrument
products.classification_rationale: Primary function is tracing and analyzing LLM application behavior in development and production → Telemetry Observability

products.description: Cloud-native ML and LLM observability platform (the commercial offering complementing the open-source Phoenix). key_dependencies: Requires an OpenTelemetry-compatible backend or uses built-in dashboard

key_dependencies: Requires an LLM-powered application to instrument

Closed-source SaaS with no self-hosted option.

products.classification_rationale: Primary function is production monitoring of LLM API calls — costs, latency, error rates → Telemetry Observability

key_dependencies: Best used with Weights & Biases platform
products.classification_rationale: Primary function is tracing and monitoring AI application behavior in development and production → Telemetry Observability

Funded by a16z.

Enterprise-focused with notable customers in financial services and healthcare.
products.classification_rationale: Production monitoring and prompt analytics for LLM applications — helps teams understand and improve LLM behavior → Telemetry Observability

Enables prompt versioning, A/B testing, and analytics. One of the earliest LLM monitoring tools (launched early 2023), focused on the prompt lifecycle rather than full tracing. 762 GitHub stars on the client library.
key_dependencies: Requires LLM API calls to route through PromptLayer
products.classification_rationale: Primary function is logging and analyzing LLM prompts and responses in production — prompt analytics and cost tracking → Telemetry Observability

For organizations already on New Relic who want AI observability unified with their existing APM, infrastructure, and log monitoring.
products.classification_rationale: LLM-specific monitoring within an enterprise APM platform — production observability for AI systems → Telemetry Observability

Leverages Dynatrace's Davis AI engine for automated root cause analysis of LLM application issues. Targets large enterprises with existing Dynatrace deployments.
products.classification_rationale: LLM-specific observability within an enterprise platform — production monitoring and debugging for AI systems → Telemetry Observability

products.description: AI observability platform for monitoring ML models and LLM applications in production. Provides data drift detection, performance monitoring, and LLM security guardrails. Built on the open-source whylogs profiling library and LangKit LLM monitoring toolkit. Differentiated by statistical profiling approach — monitors distributions rather than individual requests, enabling cost-effective monitoring at scale.
key_dependencies: Uses open-source whylogs/LangKit for data collection
products.classification_rationale: Production monitoring platform for ML/LLM systems with drift detection and security guardrails → Telemetry Observability

products.description: AI observability and reliability platform that combines offline evals, online production guardrails, and tracing — powered by their proprietary Luna-2 small judge models that detect hallucinations, tool errors, and policy violations at claimed 97% lower cost than LLM-as-judge. Positions as 'don't just monitor AI failures, stop them' and is consistently ranked in top-5 LLM observability platforms (Maxim, Firecrawl roundups). Series B-funded, with enterprise customers across financial services and healthcare.
products.classification_rationale: Hero positioning is production monitoring + guardrails (Luna-2 small judge models deployed online at 97% lower cost). Offline evaluation is a feature, not the headline. Per the litmus test 'does this tool help me understand what my LLM system is doing in production?' — yes. Belongs in Telemetry Observability.

products.description: Hosted SaaS layered on the open-source DeepEval library — adds dataset management, regression tracking, human annotation, custom dashboards, online evals against live traffic, alerting, and incident response. DeepEval itself runs 2M evals/day with 3M monthly downloads and 12.6K GitHub stars; enterprise customers on the cloud product include Microsoft, AstraZeneca, AXA, and BCG. YC W25, $2.2M seed.
products.classification_rationale: Product hero: 'Eval-First LLM Observability. Not Another APM.' Dominant feature surface is production tracing, online evals against live traffic, alerting, and incident response — observability, not benchmark running. DeepEval (the OSS library) remains in Cat 6; the cloud product belongs here.

products.description: Open-source platform for ML and GenAI lifecycle management — experiment tracking, model registry, evaluation, and (since MLflow 3.0) GenAI tracing and production observability for agents and LLM apps. Originated at Databricks (2018) and now an LF AI & Data project under Apache 2.0. The most widely adopted experiment tracking and ML observability tool by a wide margin: 30M+ monthly PyPI downloads, 26K+ GitHub stars, 900+ contributors, trusted by Databricks, Microsoft, Meta, Toyota, Booking.com, Accenture, Zillow, and Walmart. key_dependencies: Requires an ML or LLM workload to instrument
